# Example datasets

Two example datasets ship with the package, one per station type. They
are raw station exports, before any processing.

```{r function-datasets}
#' Example Visits from NEDAP Feeding Stations
#'
#' Raw visit records exported from two NEDAP feeding stations.
#'
#' @filename datasets
#'
#' @format A data frame with 31,863 rows and 9 columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{animal_number}{Full animal number.}
#'   \item{lifenumber}{Life number (empty in this export).}
#'   \item{responder}{Transponder number. `NA` for visits where no
#'     transponder was read (unidentified visits, 211 rows).}
#'   \item{location}{Station (feeder) number, 101 or 102.}
#'   \item{visit_time}{Entrance time, POSIXct in UTC.}
#'   \item{duration}{Occupation time of the visit in seconds.}
#'   \item{state}{Station state code.}
#'   \item{weight}{Body weight in grams. `0` means no valid weight.}
#'   \item{feed_intake}{Feed intake of the visit in grams.}
#' }
#' @source Pig performance testing station, 2024-02-19 to 2024-05-25,
#'   30 pigs.
"nedap"

#' Example Visits from FIRE Feeding Stations
#'
#' Raw visit records exported from two FIRE (Osborne) feeding stations.
#'
#' @format A data frame with 9,794 rows and 10 columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{Location}{Station (feeder) number, 101 or 102.}
#'   \item{Tag}{Transponder number. `0` for unidentified visits (51 rows).}
#'   \item{Date}{Visit date, `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.}
#'   \item{Entry, Exit}{Entrance and exit clock time, `"HH:MM:SS"`. A visit
#'     that crosses midnight has `Exit < Entry` (68 rows).}
#'   \item{Ent Wt, Ext Wt}{Feed trough weight at entrance and exit, kg.}
#'   \item{Consumed}{Feed intake of the visit, kg.}
#'   \item{Weight}{Body weight, kg. `0` means no valid weight.}
#'   \item{Topup Amount}{Feed dispensed into the trough during the visit, kg.}
#' }
#' @source Pig performance testing station, 2023-12-19 to 2024-02-22,
#'   26 pigs.
"fire"
```

```{r tests-datasets}
test_that("example datasets have the documented structure", {
  expect_equal(dim(nedap), c(31863L, 9L))
  expect_equal(dim(fire), c(9794L, 10L))
  expect_equal(sum(is.na(nedap$responder)), 211L)
  expect_equal(sum(fire$Tag == 0), 51L)
  expect_s3_class(nedap$visit_time, "POSIXct")
})
```

# Internal helpers

Small internal tools shared by every function of the package:

- **verbosity**: every exported function has `verbose = 0/1/2`
  (silent / summary / details). Messages go through `ppt_msg()`.
- **input checks**: `as_dt()` always returns a copy, so user objects are
  never modified; `check_cols()` reports missing columns.
- **per-pig fitting**: `fit_by_pig()` runs a function on each pig. A pig
  that fails is recorded and skipped instead of stopping everything.
- **removal log**: `new_removed()` builds the `removed` table returned by
  every analysis step.
- **result object**: `new_ppt_result()` gives every `calc_*()` function the
  same return structure.

```{r function-utils}
#' @filename utils
#' @import data.table
#' @importFrom cli cli_abort cli_warn
#' @importFrom utils globalVariables
#' @keywords internal
"_PACKAGE"

# ---- verbosity --------------------------------------------------------------

ppt_verbose <- function() {
  getOption("tidypptsda.verbose", 1L)
}

check_verbose <- function(verbose) {
  if (!is.numeric(verbose) || length(verbose) != 1L || is.na(verbose) ||
      !verbose %in% 0:2) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg verbose} must be 0 (silent), 1 (summary) or 2 (details).")
  }
  as.integer(verbose)
}

# Set the verbosity level until the calling function exits.
local_verbose <- function(verbose, envir = parent.frame()) {
  verbose <- check_verbose(verbose)
  # data.table's own "Processed ... groups" progress is not cli-styled and
  # cannot be silenced by verbose, so switch it off as well.
  old <- options(tidypptsda.verbose = verbose, datatable.showProgress = FALSE)
  do.call(on.exit, list(bquote(options(.(old))), add = TRUE), envir = envir)
  invisible(verbose)
}

# Print a message if the current verbosity is at least `level`.
ppt_msg <- function(msg,
                    type = c("info", "success", "warning", "danger",
                             "bullets", "h1", "h2"),
                    level = 1L,
                    .envir = parent.frame()) {
  if (ppt_verbose() < level) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  type <- match.arg(type)
  switch(type,
    info    = cli::cli_alert_info(msg, .envir = .envir),
    success = cli::cli_alert_success(msg, .envir = .envir),
    warning = cli::cli_alert_warning(msg, .envir = .envir),
    danger  = cli::cli_alert_danger(msg, .envir = .envir),
    bullets = cli::cli_bullets(msg, .envir = .envir),
    h1      = cli::cli_h1(msg, .envir = .envir),
    h2      = cli::cli_h2(msg, .envir = .envir)
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Show a warning alert at the point where it happens (cli style), instead of
# an R warning that is only printed after the whole call has finished.
# Whatever triggers it is also recorded in the result (removed / flags), so
# nothing is lost when silent.
ppt_warn <- function(msg, .envir = parent.frame()) {
  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L) {
    cli::cli_alert_warning(msg, .envir = .envir)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# ---- input checks -----------------------------------------------------------

# Always return a data.table that is a copy of the input.
as_dt <- function(data, arg = "data") {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg {arg}} must be a data.frame or data.table, not {.cls {class(data)[1]}}.")
  }
  if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data.table::copy(data) else data.table::as.data.table(data)
}

check_cols <- function(data, cols, arg = "data", hint = NULL) {
  missing_cols <- setdiff(cols, names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "{.arg {arg}} is missing required column{?s}: {.val {missing_cols}}.",
      "i" = hint
    ))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# ---- per-pig fitting --------------------------------------------------------

# ---- parallel computing -----------------------------------------------------

check_cores <- function(cores) {
  if (!is.numeric(cores) || length(cores) != 1L || is.na(cores) || cores < 1) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg cores} must be a single number >= 1.")
  }
  max_cores <- parallel::detectCores()
  if (is.na(max_cores)) max_cores <- 1L
  as.integer(min(cores, max_cores))
}

# Set the number of cores used by fit_by_pig() until the calling function
# exits.
local_cores <- function(cores, envir = parent.frame()) {
  cores <- check_cores(cores)
  old <- options(tidypptsda.cores = cores)
  do.call(on.exit, list(bquote(options(.(old))), add = TRUE), envir = envir)
  invisible(cores)
}

# Apply `fun` to each pig. Errors are recorded in `failed` and the pig is
# skipped; warnings are recorded in `warnings` and muffled.
# `fun` must return a data.frame (or NULL to drop the pig silently).
# Pigs are processed in parallel when option tidypptsda.cores > 1.
fit_by_pig <- function(data, fun, step, by = "responder", ...) {
  groups <- split(data, by = by, keep.by = TRUE, sorted = TRUE)
  n <- length(groups)
  args <- list(...)

  one_pig <- pig_runner(fun, args)

  cores <- min(getOption("tidypptsda.cores", 1L), n)
  runs <- run_with_progress(groups, one_pig, cores = cores,
                            label = paste0(step, ": fitting pigs"))

  out <- vector("list", n)
  failed <- vector("list", n)
  warns <- vector("list", n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    id <- as.character(groups[[i]][[by]][1L])
    res <- runs[[i]]$res
    w <- runs[[i]]$warnings
    if (length(w) > 0L) {
      warns[[i]] <- data.table::data.table(responder = id, step = step, message = w)
    }
    if (inherits(res, "error")) {
      failed[[i]] <- data.table::data.table(responder = id, step = step,
                                            reason = conditionMessage(res))
      next
    }
    if (is.null(res)) next
    res <- data.table::as.data.table(res)
    if (!by %in% names(res)) {
      res[, (by) := id]
      data.table::setcolorder(res, by)
    }
    out[[i]] <- res
  }

  failed <- data.table::rbindlist(failed)
  if (nrow(failed) == 0L) {
    failed <- data.table::data.table(responder = character(), step = character(),
                                     reason = character())
  }
  warns <- data.table::rbindlist(warns)
  if (nrow(warns) == 0L) {
    warns <- data.table::data.table(responder = character(), step = character(),
                                    message = character())
  }
  list(
    result = data.table::rbindlist(out, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE),
    failed = failed,
    warnings = warns
  )
}

# Wrap `fun` for one pig: errors are returned, warnings collected. Built by a
# top-level function so that the closure sent to parallel workers does not
# carry the data of all pigs.
pig_runner <- function(fun, args) {
  force(fun)
  force(args)
  function(g) {
    w <- character()
    res <- withCallingHandlers(
      tryCatch(do.call(fun, c(list(g), args)), error = function(e) e),
      warning = function(cnd) {
        w <<- c(w, conditionMessage(cnd))
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    )
    list(res = res, warnings = unique(w))
  }
}

# lapply(x, fun) with a cli progress bar (shown when verbose >= 1 and the
# work takes more than 2 s). With cores > 1 the items run in parallel:
# - Linux/macOS: one forked process per core works through its share; each
#   finished item is counted in a small file that the bar reads, so the bar
#   moves while the work runs and only `cores` processes are started;
# - Windows: a PSOCK cluster (needs the installed package) runs the items in
#   10 chunks, and the bar moves after each chunk.
run_with_progress <- function(x, fun, cores = 1L, label = "Working", ...) {
  n <- length(x)
  if (n == 0L) return(list())
  show <- ppt_verbose() >= 1L && n > 1L
  bar <- if (show) {
    cli::cli_progress_bar(label, total = n, clear = TRUE, .envir = environment())
  }
  set_bar <- function(k) if (show) cli::cli_progress_update(set = k, id = bar, .envir = environment())
  out <- if (cores > 1L && .Platform$OS.type != "windows") {
    run_forked(x, fun, cores, set_bar, ...)
  } else {
    if (cores > 1L) {
      check_psock()
      cl <- parallel::makeCluster(cores)
      on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl), add = TRUE)
      parallel::clusterCall(cl, function(p) invisible(.libPaths(p)), .libPaths())
      ok <- unlist(parallel::clusterCall(cl, requireNamespace, "tidypptsda", quietly = TRUE))
      if (!all(ok)) {
        cli::cli_abort(c("The parallel workers cannot load {.pkg tidypptsda}.",
                         "i" = "Install the package, or use {.code cores = 1}."))
      }
      size <- max(cores, ceiling(n / 10 / cores) * cores)
      run_chunk <- function(idx) parallel::parLapply(cl, x[idx], fun, ...)
    } else {
      size <- 1L
      run_chunk <- function(idx) lapply(x[idx], fun, ...)
    }
    res <- vector("list", n)
    for (idx in split(seq_len(n), ceiling(seq_len(n) / size))) {
      res[idx] <- run_chunk(idx)
      set_bar(max(idx))
    }
    res
  }
  if (show) cli::cli_progress_done(id = bar, .envir = environment())
  out
}

# A PSOCK worker loads the installed package, not one loaded with
# devtools::load_all(): stop instead of running other code.
check_psock <- function() {
  if (!is.null(asNamespace("tidypptsda")[[".__DEVTOOLS__"]])) {
    cli::cli_abort(c("{.code cores > 1} on Windows needs the installed package; it is loaded with {.fn devtools::load_all}.",
                     "i" = "Install it (e.g. {.code devtools::install()}), or use {.code cores = 1}."))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Fork one process per core (interleaved shares for an even load) and poll
# their progress files until all are done.
run_forked <- function(x, fun, cores, set_bar, ...) {
  n <- length(x)
  share <- split(seq_len(n), (seq_len(n) - 1L) %% min(cores, n))
  files <- vapply(seq_along(share), function(i) tempfile("ppt_progress_"), "")
  on.exit(unlink(files), add = TRUE)
  jobs <- lapply(seq_along(share), function(i) {
    parallel::mcparallel({
      con <- file(files[i], "wb")
      res <- lapply(x[share[[i]]], function(el) {
        r <- fun(el, ...)
        writeBin(as.raw(1L), con)
        flush(con)
        r
      })
      close(con)
      res
    }, silent = TRUE)
  })
  pids <- vapply(jobs, function(j) j$pid, integer(1))
  got <- vector("list", length(jobs))
  left <- seq_along(jobs)
  # on an interrupt (Esc / Ctrl+C) or an error, stop the workers still running
  on.exit(if (length(left) > 0L) {
    tools::pskill(pids[left], tools::SIGKILL)
    parallel::mccollect(jobs[left], wait = TRUE)   # reap them (no zombies)
  }, add = TRUE)
  while (length(left) > 0L) {
    r <- parallel::mccollect(jobs[left], wait = FALSE, timeout = 0.25)
    if (!is.null(r)) {
      for (nm in names(r)) {
        k <- match(as.integer(nm), pids)
        got[k] <- list(r[[nm]])
        left <- setdiff(left, k)
      }
    }
    set_bar(sum(file.size(files), na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  out <- vector("list", n)
  for (k in seq_along(share)) {
    res <- got[[k]]
    if (inherits(res, "try-error") || is.null(res)) {
      msg <- if (inherits(res, "try-error")) as.character(res) else "parallel worker failed"
      res <- rep(list(list(res = simpleError(msg), warnings = character())), length(share[[k]]))
    }
    out[share[[k]]] <- res
  }
  out
}

# ---- removal log ------------------------------------------------------------

# Each analysis step appends rows to this table: which pig was removed, at
# which step and why.
new_removed <- function(responder = character(), location = NA_character_,
                        step = character(), reason = character()) {
  if (length(responder) == 0L) {
    return(data.table::data.table(responder = character(), location = character(),
                                  step = character(), reason = character()))
  }
  data.table::data.table(
    responder = as.character(responder),
    location = as.character(location),
    step = as.character(step),
    reason = as.character(reason)
  )
}

# ---- result object ----------------------------------------------------------

new_ppt_result <- function(per_pig, daily, removed = new_removed(),
                           settings = list(), class) {
  structure(
    list(per_pig = per_pig, daily = daily, removed = removed,
         settings = settings),
    class = c(class, "ppt_result")
  )
}

#' @export
print.ppt_result <- function(x, ...) {
  cli::cli_h2("{.cls {class(x)[1]}}")
  pp <- x$per_pig
  if (!is.null(pp) && "status" %in% names(pp)) {
    st <- table(factor(pp$status, levels = c("keep", "low_confidence", "removed")))
    cli::cli_text("Pigs: {nrow(pp)} (keep {st[['keep']]}, low confidence {st[['low_confidence']]}, removed {st[['removed']]})")
  } else if (!is.null(pp)) {
    cli::cli_text("Pigs: {nrow(pp)}")
  }
  for (nm in setdiff(names(x), "settings")) {
    el <- x[[nm]]
    if (is.data.frame(el)) cli::cli_text("{.field ${nm}}: {nrow(el)} row{?s} x {ncol(el)} column{?s}")
  }
  invisible(x)
}

# ---- colours ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Okabe-Ito palette: colour-blind safe, no extra dependency.
ppt_palette <- function(n) {
  pal <- c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00",
           "#56B4E9", "#F0E442", "#000000", "#999999")
  if (n > length(pal)) {
    pal <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(pal)(n)
  }
  pal[seq_len(n)]
}
```

```{r tests-utils}
test_that("as_dt returns a copy and never modifies the input", {
  dt <- data.table::data.table(a = 1:3)
  out <- as_dt(dt)
  out[, b := 1]
  expect_false("b" %in% names(dt))
  expect_s3_class(as_dt(data.frame(a = 1)), "data.table")
  expect_error(as_dt(1:3), "data.frame")
})

test_that("check_cols names the missing columns", {
  expect_true(check_cols(data.frame(a = 1, b = 2), c("a", "b")))
  expect_error(check_cols(data.frame(a = 1), c("a", "b", "c")), "b")
})

test_that("verbosity is validated and restored on exit", {
  expect_error(check_verbose(3), "verbose")
  expect_error(check_verbose(TRUE), "verbose")
  f <- function() {
    local_verbose(0)
    ppt_verbose()
  }
  old <- getOption("tidypptsda.verbose")
  expect_equal(f(), 0L)
  expect_identical(getOption("tidypptsda.verbose"), old)
})

test_that("ppt_msg and ppt_warn respect verbose", {
  silent <- function() {
    local_verbose(0)
    ppt_msg("hidden")
    ppt_warn("hidden")
    "done"
  }
  expect_silent(silent())
  warn_now <- function() {
    local_verbose(1)
    ppt_warn("shown at once")
  }
  expect_message(warn_now(), "shown at once")
  expect_no_warning(suppressMessages(warn_now()))
  loud <- function() {
    local_verbose(1)
    ppt_msg("shown")
  }
  expect_message(loud(), "shown")
  detail <- function(v) {
    local_verbose(v)
    ppt_msg("detail only", level = 2)
  }
  expect_silent(detail(1))
  expect_message(detail(2), "detail only")
})

test_that("fit_by_pig isolates failures and records warnings", {
  dt <- data.table::data.table(responder = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 3),
                               x = 1:9)
  f <- function(d) {
    if (d$responder[1] == "b") stop("too few points")
    if (d$responder[1] == "c") warning("did not converge")
    data.frame(mean_x = mean(d$x))
  }
  res <- fit_by_pig(dt, f, step = "test")
  expect_equal(res$result$responder, c("a", "c"))
  expect_equal(res$result$mean_x, c(2, 8))
  expect_equal(res$failed$responder, "b")
  expect_match(res$failed$reason, "too few points")
  expect_equal(res$warnings$responder, "c")
  expect_match(res$warnings$message, "converge")
  # no failures: empty tables keep their columns
  ok <- fit_by_pig(dt[responder == "a"], f, step = "test")
  expect_named(ok$failed, c("responder", "step", "reason"))
  expect_named(ok$warnings, c("responder", "step", "message"))
})

test_that("new_removed builds a consistent log", {
  empty <- new_removed()
  expect_equal(nrow(empty), 0L)
  expect_named(empty, c("responder", "location", "step", "reason"))
  log <- new_removed(c(1, 2), "101", "weight_range", "too light")
  expect_type(log$responder, "character")
  expect_equal(nrow(log), 2L)
})

test_that("ppt_palette returns n colours", {
  expect_length(ppt_palette(3), 3L)
  expect_length(ppt_palette(15), 15L)
})

test_that("PSOCK workers need the installed package", {
  if (is.null(asNamespace("tidypptsda")[[".__DEVTOOLS__"]])) {
    expect_true(check_psock())
  } else {
    expect_error(check_psock(), "load_all")
  }
})
```

# qc_config

All quality-control thresholds live in one object created by `qc_config()`.
Any single parameter can be overridden.

```{r function-qc_config}
#' Build Quality-Control Settings
#'
#' @description
#' Build the set of quality-control (QC) thresholds used by the whole
#' pipeline. Every parameter has a default; override any of them through
#' `...`.
#'
#' @param ... Parameters to override, as `name = value`. See **Parameters**.
#'
#' @section Parameters:
#' **Station transfer and test interruptions** (see [prep_visits()])
#' - `misread_max_visits`: a run of at most this many consecutive visits at
#'   another station, inside the pig's visits at its current station, is a
#'   transponder misread: the visits are kept as unidentified visits.
#'   Default 2.
#' - `max_gap_days`: a pig without any visit for longer than this (e.g.
#'   isolated for treatment, at any station or between two stations) is
#'   flagged as low confidence by [clean_weight()]. Default 3.
#' - `max_jump_kg`: body weight jump at a station transfer, beyond the
#'   expected growth over the gap, that gives a warning and flags the pig as
#'   low confidence. Default 10.
#'
#' **Body weight records** (used by [clean_weight()], in this order)
#' - `weight_range`: valid body weight of a single record, kg. Default
#'   `c(15, 150)`.
#' - `adapt_days`: adaptation period after entry, days (default 7). Body
#'   weights of the first `adapt_days` days after a pig's first visit are
#'   not used (`qc_flag = "adaptation"`). Their feed intake is kept: it
#'   counts for ADFI and FCR when these days lie inside `stage_range` (e.g. a
#'   pig that enters at 45 kg with a 30-120 kg stage), and not when the pig
#'   is still below the stage. 0 = off.
#' - `weight_track`: track the weight of each pig back from the end of the
#'   test (default `TRUE`). The scale only counts a pig standing on it with
#'   all four feet, so a reading is too light only rarely, while several
#'   small pigs on the scale at once give readings that are too heavy. At
#'   the end of the test the pigs are large and only one fits on the scale,
#'   so the last days are the most reliable. Starting from the median of the
#'   last 3 recorded days and the daily gain of the last 14 days, the weight
#'   is tracked back day by day: a record is kept when it lies within
#'   `track_tol` (default 8%, at least 2 kg, widened by 0.5 kg per day
#'   without kept records) of the weight expected for that day; the daily
#'   gain is updated from the kept daily weights of the next 10 days. Other
#'   records are removed (`qc_flag = "track"`). Pigs with less than 7
#'   recorded days or a test shorter than 14 days are not tracked.
#' - `weight_outlier`: outlier methods applied to the remaining records, one
#'   or more of `"rlm"` (quadratic robust regression, bisquare weights; a
#'   record with a weight below `rlm_cutoff` is an outlier), `"loess"`
#'   (robust LOESS smooth; a record more than `sd_max` robust SDs from it is
#'   an outlier), `"stl"` (trend + weekly component of the daily median
#'   weight) and `"sd"` (quadratic least squares, `sd_max` SDs). Default
#'   `c("rlm", "loess")`.
#' - `outlier_combine`: `"any"` (outlier for any method, default) or
#'   `"majority"`.
#' - `rlm_cutoff`: default 0.5.
#' - `sd_max`: default 3.
#' - `loess_span`: smoothing span for LOESS and STL. Default 0.75.
#'
#' **Pig-level checks** (used by [clean_weight()])
#' - `min_records`, `min_test_days`, `max_missing_rate`: a pig with fewer
#'   valid weights (default 20), a shorter test (default 35 days) or a larger
#'   share of test days without a valid weight (default 0.30) is removed.
#' - `entry_weight_max`, `exit_weight_min`: a pig entering heavier (default
#'   65 kg) or leaving lighter (default 85 kg) is flagged as low confidence.
#' - `track_flag_share`: a pig whose tracking removes more than this share of
#'   its records (default 0.4) is flagged as low confidence: the scale
#'   probably did not weigh it correctly for a long time (e.g. a faulty load
#'   cell).
#' - `smooth_r2_min`: a pig whose valid weights fit their LOESS smooth with
#'   an R² below this (default 0.99) is flagged as low confidence.
#'
#' **Growth, filled weights and ADG** (used by [calc_adg()])
#' - `stage_range`: body weight interval for ADG, ADFI and FCR, kg. Default
#'   `c(30, 120)`.
#' - `curve_model`: growth curve that fixes the stage start and end and fills
#'   the weights before the first and after the last recorded day:
#'   `"poly2"` (default), `"poly1"`, `"poly3"` or `"gompertz"` (falls back
#'   to `"poly2"` when it does not converge). Missing days between recorded
#'   days are always filled by linear interpolation.
#' - `max_extrap_days`: maximum extrapolation of the curve, days. Default 30.
#' - `curve_extrap`: how the curve continues beyond the records.
#'   `"start"` (default): before the first record a straight line from the
#'   curve at the first record, with the robust slope of the records of the
#'   first 14 days (limited to 0.2-1.5 kg/d); after the last record the
#'   fitted curve itself. `"tangent"`: such a line at both ends; `"curve"`:
#'   the fitted curve at both ends (before version 1.4.0). A polynomial
#'   bends away from the data when it is extrapolated for weeks; the
#'   tangent does not. At the end the tangent gave better ADG but a worse
#'   FCR ranking (the feed of the extrapolated days follows the higher
#'   weights), hence `"start"`. Compare them on your data with
#'   [validate_truncation()].
#'
#' **Feeder errors** (Casey et al. 2005, Table 3)
#' - `fiv_range`: FIV-lo / FIV-hi, feed intake per visit, g.
#' - `fiv0_abs_max`: FIV-0, maximum |FIV| for a 0 s visit, g.
#' - `duration_max`: OTV-hi, maximum occupation time per visit, s.
#' - `speed_fiv_lo_max`: FRV-hi-FIV-lo, maximum feeding rate for visits with
#'   0 < FIV < 50 g, g/min.
#' - `speed_strict_max`: FRV-hi-strict, maximum feeding rate when the
#'   preceding or following visit has FIV < -20 g, g/min.
#' - `speed_range`: FRV-lo and FRV-hi, g/min.
#' - `idle_duration_max`: FRV-0, maximum occupation time with no intake, s.
#' - `trough_diff_range`: LWD / FWD, trough weight difference between
#'   subsequent visits, g.
#' - `max_unidentified_feed_kg`: feed disappearance in unidentified visits
#'   per feeder above which a warning is given.
#' - `fiv_max_by_weight`: optional table that replaces the upper limit of
#'   `fiv_range` (FIV-hi) by a limit that depends on body weight, and
#'   optionally on breed. Columns `weight_from` (kg, lower bound of the
#'   weight class), `fiv_max` (g) and optionally `breed`. See
#'   [fiv_max_example()]. `NULL` = off.
#'
#' **Daily feed intake** (used by [calc_adfi()])
#' - `dfi_range`: valid daily feed intake, kg.
#' - `dfi_quantile`: optional, lower and upper quantile cut-offs (e.g.
#'   `c(0.025, 0.99)`). `NULL` = off.
#' - `dfi_correct`: `"lmm"` (Jiao et al. 2014) or `"none"`.
#' - `impute_method`: how missing stage days are filled. Gaps between
#'   recorded days of up to `long_gap_days` days are filled from a robust
#'   LOESS smooth of the daily intake (`"loess_pop"`, `"loess_lm"`); longer
#'   gaps and the days before the first / after the last recorded day:
#'   `"loess_pop"` (default): longer gaps and the days before the first
#'   recorded day from the population curve of daily intake on body weight
#'   (all pigs, or each breed), scaled to the intake level of the pig; the
#'   days after the last recorded day from a linear regression of the pig's
#'   own daily intake on body weight; `"loess_lm"`: the pig's own regression
#'   for all of these; `"linear"`: linear interpolation between recorded
#'   days whatever the gap, the per-pig regression at the ends.
#' - `long_gap_days`: default 3.
#'
#' **Confidence flags** (used by [calc_fcr()])
#' - `max_edge_extrap_days`: a pig is `"low_confidence"` when its weights or
#'   its feed intake are filled over more than this many days at the start
#'   or the end of the stage. Default 15.
#' - `min_coverage`: minimum share of stage days with recorded feed intake.
#'   Default 0.7.
#' - `bin_width`: width of the body weight classes used for the segment
#'   checks of [calc_fcr()], kg. Default 10.
#' - `min_bin_coverage_kg`: an inner weight class whose recorded body
#'   weights span less than this many kg flags the pig. Default 6.
#' - `bin_fcr_limits`: optional table of plausible FCR per weight class,
#'   columns `weight_from` (kg), `fcr_min`, `fcr_max`. See
#'   [bin_fcr_example()]. `NULL` = off.
#'
#' @return An object of class `ppt_qc`: a named list of parameters.
#'
#' @references
#' Casey, D. S., Stern, H. S., & Dekkers, J. C. M. (2005). Identification of
#' errors and factors associated with errors in data from electronic swine
#' feeders. *Journal of Animal Science*, 83, 969-982.
#'
#' Jiao, S., Maltecca, C., Gray, K. A., & Cassady, J. P. (2014). Feed intake,
#' average daily gain, feed efficiency, and real-time ultrasound traits in
#' Duroc pigs: I. *Journal of Animal Science*, 92, 2377-2386.
#'
#' @filename qc_config
#' @export
qc_config <- function(...) {
  cfg <- qc_defaults()
  overrides <- list(...)
  if (length(overrides) > 0L) {
    nms <- names(overrides)
    if (is.null(nms) || any(!nzchar(nms))) {
      unnamed <- overrides[if (is.null(nms)) seq_along(overrides) else !nzchar(nms)]
      if (any(vapply(unnamed, function(x) is.character(x) && length(x) == 1L, logical(1)))) {
        cli::cli_abort(c("The presets {.val casey}, {.val national} and {.val legacy} were removed in tidypptsda 1.0.0.",
                         "i" = "Use {.code qc_config()} and override single parameters, e.g. {.code qc_config(duration_max = 1800)}."))
      }
      cli::cli_abort("All parameters in {.arg ...} must be named.")
    }
    if ("max_overlap_days" %in% nms) {
      cli::cli_abort(c("{.arg max_overlap_days} was removed in tidypptsda 1.2.0.",
                       "i" = "Misreads are now found by run length: see {.arg misread_max_visits} (default 2)."))
    }
    unknown <- setdiff(nms, names(cfg))
    if (length(unknown) > 0L) {
      hints <- vapply(unknown, function(u) {
        m <- agrep(u, names(cfg), max.distance = 0.3, value = TRUE)
        if (length(m) > 0L) paste0("did you mean {.val ", m[1L], "}?") else ""
      }, character(1))
      cli::cli_abort(c(
        "Unknown QC parameter{?s}: {.val {unknown}}.",
        stats::setNames(hints[nzchar(hints)], rep("i", sum(nzchar(hints))))
      ))
    }
    cfg <- qc_set(cfg, overrides)
  }
  qc_validate(cfg)
  structure(cfg, class = "ppt_qc")
}

#' @export
print.ppt_qc <- function(x, ...) {
  cli::cli_h2("QC settings")
  groups <- qc_groups()
  fmt <- function(v) {
    if (is.null(v)) return("NULL (off)")
    if (is.data.frame(v)) return(sprintf("table (%d rows)", nrow(v)))
    paste(format(v), collapse = ", ")
  }
  for (g in unique(groups)) {
    cli::cli_text("{.strong {g}}")
    nms <- names(groups)[groups == g]
    lines <- vapply(nms, function(nm) paste0("{.field ", nm, "}: ", fmt(x[[nm]])), character(1))
    cli::cli_bullets(stats::setNames(lines, rep(" ", length(lines))))
  }
  invisible(x)
}

#' Example threshold tables
#'
#' @description
#' Example tables for the optional QC parameters `fiv_max_by_weight` and
#' `bin_fcr_limits` of [qc_config()].
#'
#' - `fiv_max_example()`: maximum feed intake per visit (g) by breed
#'   (`"YY"`, `"LL"`, `"DD"`) and 10 kg body weight class from 20 to 140 kg.
#' - `bin_fcr_example()`: plausible feed conversion ratio per 10 kg body
#'   weight class from 30 to 120 kg.
#'
#' The values come from in-house quality-control scripts of a pig testing
#' station, not from the literature. Check them against your own data
#' before use.
#'
#' @return A `data.table`. `fiv_max_example()`: `breed`, `weight_from`
#'   (kg), `fiv_max` (g). `bin_fcr_example()`: `weight_from` (kg),
#'   `fcr_min`, `fcr_max`.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' fiv_max_example()
#' qc <- qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = fiv_max_example(),
#'                 bin_fcr_limits = bin_fcr_example())
fiv_max_example <- function() {
  w <- seq(20, 130, by = 10)
  data.table::data.table(
    breed = rep(c("YY", "LL", "DD"), each = length(w)),
    weight_from = rep(w, 3L),
    fiv_max = c(747.0, 936.0, 1125.1, 1314.1, 1503.2, 1692.2, 1881.2, 2070.3, 2259.3, 2448.4, 2637.4, 2826.5,
                821.6, 1044.8, 1268.0, 1491.2, 1714.4, 1937.7, 2160.9, 2384.1, 2607.3, 2830.5, 3053.7, 3277.0,
                712.6, 916.9, 1121.2, 1325.4, 1529.7, 1734.0, 1938.2, 2142.5, 2346.8, 2551.0, 2755.3, 2959.6)
  )
}

#' @rdname fiv_max_example
#' @export
bin_fcr_example <- function() {
  data.table::data.table(
    weight_from = seq(30, 110, by = 10),
    fcr_min = c(0.76, 1.06, 1.14, 1.28, 1.35, 1.36, 1.34, 1.34, 1.31),
    fcr_max = c(3.16, 3.08, 3.30, 3.41, 3.59, 3.86, 4.12, 4.27, 4.50)
  )
}

# Assign values one by one so that NULL values are kept, not dropped.
qc_set <- function(cfg, values) {
  for (nm in names(values)) {
    cfg[nm] <- list(values[[nm]])
  }
  cfg
}

    sd_max = 3,

    # pig-level checks

    exit_weight_min = 85,

    # growth, filled weights and ADG
    stage_range = c(30, 120),

    max_extrap_days = 30,
    curve_extrap = "start",
    # feeder errors, Casey et al. (2005) Table 3
    fiv_range = c(-20, 2000),

    duration_max = 3600,
    speed_fiv_lo_max = 500,
    speed_strict_max = 110,
    speed_range = c(2, 170),
    idle_duration_max = 500,

    bin_width = 10,
    min_bin_coverage_kg = 6,
    bin_fcr_limits = NULL
  )
}

# Validation rules for each parameter.
qc_spec <- function() {
  num <- function(min = -Inf, max = Inf, null = FALSE) list(type = "num", min = min, max = max, null = null)
  rng <- function(min = -Inf, max = Inf, null = FALSE) list(type = "range", min = min, max = max, null = null)
  chc <- function(choices, multiple = FALSE) list(type = "choice", choices = choices, multiple = multiple, null = FALSE)
  tbl <- function(cols, optional = character()) list(type = "table", cols = cols, optional = optional, null = TRUE)
  lgl <- function() list(type = "logical", null = FALSE)
  list(
    misread_max_visits = num(0), max_gap_days = num(0), max_jump_kg = num(0),
    weight_range = rng(0), adapt_days = num(0), weight_track = lgl(), track_tol = num(0, 1),
    weight_outlier = chc(c("rlm", "loess", "stl", "sd"), multiple = TRUE),
    outlier_combine = chc(c("any", "majority")),
    rlm_cutoff = num(0, 1), sd_max = num(0), loess_span = num(0.1, 1),
    min_records = num(3), min_test_days = num(1), max_missing_rate = num(0, 1),
    entry_weight_max = num(0), exit_weight_min = num(0), track_flag_share = num(0, 1),
    smooth_r2_min = num(0, 1, null = TRUE),
    stage_range = rng(0), curve_model = chc(c("poly1", "poly2", "poly3", "gompertz")),
    max_extrap_days = num(0), curve_extrap = chc(c("start", "curve", "tangent")),
    fiv_range = rng(), fiv0_abs_max = num(0), duration_max = num(0),
    speed_fiv_lo_max = num(0), speed_strict_max = num(0), speed_range = rng(0),
    idle_duration_max = num(0), trough_diff_range = rng(),
    max_unidentified_feed_kg = num(0),
    fiv_max_by_weight = tbl(c("weight_from", "fiv_max"), optional = "breed"),
    dfi_range = rng(0), dfi_quantile = rng(0, 1, null = TRUE),
    dfi_correct = chc(c("lmm", "none")),
    impute_method = chc(c("loess_pop", "loess_lm", "linear")),
    long_gap_days = num(1),
    max_edge_extrap_days = num(0), min_coverage = num(0, 1),
    bin_width = num(1), min_bin_coverage_kg = num(0),
    bin_fcr_limits = tbl(c("weight_from", "fcr_min", "fcr_max"))
  )
}

qc_validate <- function(cfg) {
  spec <- qc_spec()
  for (nm in names(spec)) {
    s <- spec[[nm]]
    v <- cfg[[nm]]
    if (is.null(v)) {
      if (!s$null) cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} cannot be NULL.")
      next
    }
    if (s$type == "num") {
      if (!is.numeric(v) || length(v) != 1L || is.na(v) || v < s$min || v > s$max) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be a single number between {s$min} and {s$max}, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    } else if (s$type == "range") {
      if (!is.numeric(v) || length(v) != 2L || anyNA(v) || v[1L] >= v[2L] ||
          any(v < s$min) || any(v > s$max)) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be two increasing numbers between {s$min} and {s$max}, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    } else if (s$type == "table") {
      check_qc_table(v, nm, s$cols, s$optional)
    } else if (s$type == "logical") {
      if (!is.logical(v) || length(v) != 1L || is.na(v)) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be TRUE or FALSE, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    } else if (s$type == "choice") {
      ok <- is.character(v) && length(v) >= 1L && all(v %in% s$choices) &&
        (s$multiple || length(v) == 1L) && !anyDuplicated(v)
      if (!ok) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be {if (s$multiple) 'one or more of' else 'one of'} {.val {s$choices}}, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    }
  }

  # Cross-parameter consistency
  if (cfg$stage_range[1L] < cfg$weight_range[1L] || cfg$stage_range[2L] > cfg$weight_range[2L]) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field stage_range} ({cfg$stage_range[1]}-{cfg$stage_range[2]} kg) must lie inside {.field weight_range} ({cfg$weight_range[1]}-{cfg$weight_range[2]} kg).")
  }
  if (cfg$entry_weight_max >= cfg$exit_weight_min) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field entry_weight_max} must be smaller than {.field exit_weight_min}.")
  }
  if (cfg$outlier_combine == "majority" && length(cfg$weight_outlier) < 2L) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field outlier_combine = \"majority\"} needs at least two methods in {.field weight_outlier}.")
  }
  if (cfg$min_bin_coverage_kg > cfg$bin_width) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field min_bin_coverage_kg} cannot be larger than {.field bin_width}.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Table parameters: required numeric columns, optional character columns,
# one row per (optional key, weight_from).
check_qc_table <- function(v, nm, cols, optional) {
  if (!is.data.frame(v)) {
    cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be a data frame with columns {.val {cols}}.")
  }
  miss <- setdiff(cols, names(v))
  if (length(miss) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} is missing column{?s} {.val {miss}}.")
  }
  for (cl in cols) {
    if (!is.numeric(v[[cl]]) || anyNA(v[[cl]])) {
      cli::cli_abort("Column {.field {cl}} of {.field {nm}} must be numeric without NA.")
    }
  }
  if (nrow(v) == 0L) cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} has no rows.")
  keys <- intersect(optional, names(v))
  key <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(c(keys, "weight_from"), function(k) v[[k]]), sep = "|"))
  if (anyDuplicated(key)) {
    cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} has duplicated {.field weight_from} rows{if (length(keys)) ' within a breed' else ''}.")
  }
  if (all(c("fcr_min", "fcr_max") %in% names(v)) && any(v$fcr_min >= v$fcr_max)) {
    cli::cli_abort("In {.field {nm}}, {.field fcr_min} must be smaller than {.field fcr_max}.")
  }
  if ("fiv_max" %in% names(v) && any(v$fiv_max <= 0)) {
    cli::cli_abort("In {.field {nm}}, {.field fiv_max} must be positive.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

qc$duration_max

test_that("the default settings are valid", {
  q <- qc_config()
  expect_s3_class(q, "ppt_qc")
  expect_setequal(names(q), names(qc_defaults()))
  expect_equal(q$duration_max, 3600)
  expect_equal(q$speed_range, c(2, 170))
  expect_equal(q$weight_range, c(15, 150))
  expect_equal(q$weight_outlier, c("rlm", "loess"))
  expect_equal(q$adapt_days, 7)
  expect_true(q$weight_track)
  expect_equal(q$impute_method, "loess_pop")
  expect_equal(q$long_gap_days, 3)
  expect_equal(q$max_edge_extrap_days, 15)
  expect_error(qc_config(impute_method = "national"), "impute_method")
})

test_that("overrides apply and NULL switches optional rules off", {
  q <- qc_config(min_test_days = 50, smooth_r2_min = NULL)
  expect_equal(q$min_test_days, 50)
  expect_null(q$smooth_r2_min)
  expect_true("smooth_r2_min" %in% names(q))
})

test_that("unknown, unnamed parameters and old presets are rejected", {
  expect_error(qc_config(duration = 1800), "duration_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(1800), "named")
  expect_error(qc_config("national"), "removed")
  expect_error(qc_config(method = "national"), "Unknown")
})

test_that("invalid values are rejected", {
  expect_error(qc_config(duration_max = -1), "duration_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(duration_max = "1800"), "duration_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(weight_range = c(140, 25)), "weight_range")
  expect_error(qc_config(curve_model = "loess"), "curve_model")
  expect_error(qc_config(weight_outlier = c("rlm", "rlm")), "weight_outlier")
  expect_error(qc_config(rlm_cutoff = NULL), "NULL")
  expect_error(qc_config(weight_track = "yes"), "TRUE or FALSE")
})

test_that("table parameters are validated", {
  expect_silent(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = fiv_max_example(),
                          bin_fcr_limits = bin_fcr_example()))
  expect_error(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = data.frame(weight_from = 20)), "fiv_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = data.frame(weight_from = c(20, 20), fiv_max = 1:2)), "duplicated")
  expect_silent(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = data.frame(breed = c("A", "B"), weight_from = c(20, 20), fiv_max = 1:2)))
  expect_error(qc_config(bin_fcr_limits = data.frame(weight_from = 30, fcr_min = 3, fcr_max = 2)), "fcr_min")
  expect_error(qc_config(bin_fcr_limits = "x"), "data frame")
  expect_error(qc_config(min_bin_coverage_kg = 12), "bin_width")

})

})

test_that("the removed max_overlap_days says what to use", {

# read_station

`read_station()` reads one or many station export files (or a whole
folder) and returns **one standard table**: the same column names, types
and units for NEDAP and FIRE, ready for [prep_visits()].

Which column of the export holds which field is described by a **station
format**. The package has a built-in format for each station type, so the
usual exports need no setup. For an export with other column names or
positions (another software version, Chinese headers, another device),
write the format once as a small tab-separated file and pass it with
`format`. `station_format("fire", file = "fire_format.txt")` writes the
built-in format as a template to start from.

```{r function-read_station}
#' Read Feeding Station Export Files
#'
#' @description
#' Read one or more NEDAP or FIRE exports (CSV, TXT or Excel), map their
#' columns to the standard fields with a station format, and combine them
#' into one standard table for [prep_visits()].
#'
#' @param files Character vector of file paths, or a single folder. For a
#'   folder, all files matching `pattern` are read.
#' @param station `"nedap"`, `"fire"` or `NULL` (default). With `NULL`, the
#'   station type is detected by trying the built-in formats on the column
#'   names. Required when `format` is given.
#' @param format `NULL` (default) for the built-in format of `station`, or a
#'   station format: the path of a tab-separated format file, or a data
#'   frame with columns `field`, `column` and optionally `unit` (see
#'   [station_format()]).
#' @param pattern Regular expression for file names when `files` is a
#'   folder. Default: CSV, TXT, XLSX and XLS files (case-insensitive).
#' @param sheet Sheet name or number for Excel files. Default `1`.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details per file).
#' @param ... Further arguments passed to [data.table::fread()] (CSV and
#'   TXT files).
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with the standard fields of the station type
#'   (see [station_format()]) plus `source_file` (file name without
#'   folder):
#'   - `responder` (character, transponder number as recorded),
#'     `location` (character), `breed` (character, if mapped);
#'   - `entry_time`, `exit_time`: POSIXct, clock time stored as UTC;
#'   - `duration`: seconds; `feed_intake`, `trough_in`, `trough_out`,
#'     `topup`: g; `weight`: kg.
#'
#'   Fields the station type does not have, or optional fields missing in
#'   the export, are `NA`. Columns of the export that are not mapped are
#'   dropped. Attribute `"station"` holds the station type and
#'   `"station_format"` the format used.
#'
#' @details
#' CSV and TXT files are read with [data.table::fread()], which detects the
#' separator (comma, tab, semicolon). Excel files need the readxl package.
#' The column mapped to `responder` is always read as text, so leading
#' zeros are kept.
#'
#' Columns are matched by name first (exact, then ignoring case and
#' surrounding spaces). A number in the format is a column position, used
#' when the export has no usable header. Positions are fragile: if the
#' export software adds a column, every later field shifts without an
#' error. Use names where possible.
#'
#' Every file must contain all required fields of the station type. A
#' missing optional field (`topup`, `breed`) is filled with `NA`.
#'
#' @seealso [station_format()] for the fields and the format file;
#'   [prep_visits()] for the next step.
#' @export
read_station <- function(files,
                         station = NULL,
                         format = NULL,
                         pattern = "\\.(csv|txt|xlsx|xls)$",
                         sheet = 1,
                         verbose = 1,
                         ...) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  files <- resolve_files(files, pattern)
  if (!is.null(station)) station <- check_station(station)
  if (!is.null(format)) {
    if (is.null(station)) {
      cli::cli_abort("Set {.arg station} when {.arg format} is given.")
    }
    fmt <- as_station_format(format, station)
  }

  ppt_msg("Reading {length(files)} file{?s}", "h1")

  # Columns read as text: the responder column(s) of the format, or of both
  # built-in formats when the station type is still unknown.
  id_specs <- if (!is.null(format)) {
    fmt[field == "responder", column]
  } else if (!is.null(station)) {
    builtin_format(station)[field == "responder", column]
  } else {
    c(builtin_format("nedap")[field == "responder", column],
      builtin_format("fire")[field == "responder", column])
  }

  tables <- lapply(files, function(f) {
    dt <- read_raw_file(f, id_specs, sheet, ...)
    ppt_msg("{.file {basename(f)}}: {nrow(dt)} rows, {ncol(dt)} columns",
            "info", level = 2)
    dt
  })
  names(tables) <- basename(files)

  # Station type: detect from the first file, then require it everywhere.
  if (is.null(station)) {
    station <- detect_station(tables[[1L]])
    ppt_msg("Detected station type {.val {station}}", "info")
  }
  if (is.null(format)) fmt <- builtin_format(station)

  std <- lapply(names(tables), function(nm) {
    apply_format(tables[[nm]], fmt, station, arg = nm)
  })
  names(std) <- names(tables)
  out <- data.table::rbindlist(std, use.names = TRUE, idcol = "source_file")
  data.table::setcolorder(out, setdiff(names(out), "source_file"))
  data.table::setattr(out, "station", station)
  data.table::setattr(out, "station_format", fmt)
  data.table::setattr(out, "ppt_standard", TRUE)

  ppt_msg("Read {nrow(out)} rows from {length(files)} file{?s} ({toupper(station)})",
          "success")
  out
}

# ---- standard fields --------------------------------------------------------

format_fields <- function() {
  data.table::data.table(
    field = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time", "duration",
              "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in", "trough_out", "topup",
              "breed"),
    type = c("text", "text", "time", "time", "duration",
             "mass_g", "mass_kg", "mass_g", "mass_g", "mass_g", "text"),
    description = c(
      "Transponder number", "Station (feeder) ID", "Entrance time",
      "Exit time", "Occupation time", "Feed intake of the visit",
      "Body weight", "Trough weight at entrance", "Trough weight at exit",
      "Feed dispensed during the visit", "Breed"
    )
  )
}

station_fields <- function(station) {
  switch(station,
    nedap = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time", "duration",
              "feed_intake", "weight", "breed"),
    fire = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time",
             "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in", "trough_out", "topup",
             "breed")
  )
}

station_required <- function(station) {
  switch(station,
    nedap = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "feed_intake", "weight"),
    fire = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time",
             "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in", "trough_out")
  )
}

builtin_format <- function(station) {
  switch(station,
    nedap = data.table::data.table(
      field = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time",
                "duration", "feed_intake", "weight", "breed"),
      column = c("responder", "location", "visit_time", "-", "duration",
                 "feed_intake", "weight", "breed"),
      unit = c("-", "-", "-", "-", "s", "g", "auto", "-")
    ),
    fire = data.table::data.table(
      field = c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time",
                "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in", "trough_out", "topup",
                "breed"),
      column = c("Tag", "Location", "Date,Entry", "Date,Exit", "Consumed",
                 "Weight", "Ent Wt", "Ext Wt", "Topup Amount", "breed"),
      unit = c("-", "-", "-", "-", "kg", "kg", "kg", "kg", "kg", "-")
    )
  )
}

# Read and check a user format: a file path, a data frame or a named
# character vector (field = column).
as_station_format <- function(format, station) {
  if (is.character(format) && length(format) == 1L && is.null(names(format))) {
    if (!file.exists(format)) cli::cli_abort("Format file not found: {.path {format}}.")
    lines <- readLines(format, encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE)
    lines <- sub("^\ufeff", "", lines)
    lines <- lines[nzchar(trimws(lines)) & !startsWith(trimws(lines), "#")]
    if (length(lines) < 2L) cli::cli_abort("Format file {.path {format}} has no fields.")
    fmt <- data.table::fread(text = paste(lines, collapse = "\n"), sep = "\t",
                             colClasses = "character", header = TRUE,
                             fill = TRUE, encoding = "UTF-8")
    src <- format
  } else if (is.character(format) && !is.null(names(format))) {
    fmt <- data.table::data.table(field = names(format), column = unname(format))
    src <- "format"
  } else if (is.data.frame(format)) {
    fmt <- data.table::as.data.table(format)
    src <- "format"
  } else {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg format} must be a file path, a data frame or a named character vector.")
  }
  data.table::setnames(fmt, tolower(trimws(names(fmt))))
  if (!all(c("field", "column") %in% names(fmt))) {
    cli::cli_abort(c("{.arg format} must have columns {.val field} and {.val column}.",
                     "i" = "Columns found: {.val {names(fmt)}}."))
  }
  if (!"unit" %in% names(fmt)) fmt[, unit := "-"]
  fmt <- fmt[, .(field = trimws(as.character(field)),
                 column = trimws(as.character(column)),
                 unit = trimws(as.character(unit)))]
  fmt[is.na(column) | column == "", column := "-"]
  fmt[is.na(unit) | unit == "", unit := "-"]

  allowed <- station_fields(station)
  bad <- setdiff(fmt$field, allowed)
  if (length(bad) > 0L) {
    hints <- vapply(bad, function(b) {
      m <- agrep(b, allowed, max.distance = 0.3, value = TRUE)
      if (length(m) > 0L) paste0(b, ": did you mean ", m[1L], "?") else b
    }, character(1))
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "Unknown field(s) for {toupper(station)} in {.path {src}}: {.val {bad}}.",
      stats::setNames(hints, rep("x", length(hints))),
      "i" = "Fields for {toupper(station)}: {.val {allowed}}."
    ))
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(fmt$field)) {
    cli::cli_abort("Field(s) given twice in {.path {src}}: {.val {unique(fmt$field[duplicated(fmt$field)])}}.")
  }
  missing_req <- setdiff(station_required(station), fmt[column != "-", field])
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "{.path {src}} has no column for required field(s) {.val {missing_req}}.",
      "i" = "See {.code station_format(\"{station}\")}."
    ))
  }
  if (station == "nedap" && !any(fmt[column != "-", field] %in% c("duration", "exit_time"))) {
    cli::cli_abort("A NEDAP format needs {.val duration} or {.val exit_time}.")
  }
  ff <- format_fields()
  types <- ff$type[match(fmt$field, ff$field)]
  ok_unit <- ifelse(
    startsWith(types, "mass"), fmt$unit %in% c("-", "kg", "g", "auto"),
    ifelse(types == "duration", fmt$unit %in% c("-", "s", "min"),
           types == "time" | fmt$unit == "-")
  )
  if (!all(ok_unit)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "Unknown unit(s) in {.path {src}}: {.val {paste(fmt$field[!ok_unit], fmt$unit[!ok_unit], sep = ' = ')}}.",
      "i" = "Masses: kg, g or auto; duration: s or min; times: - or a strptime format."
    ))
  }
  # Fields of the station not listed are absent.
  extra <- setdiff(allowed, fmt$field)
  if (length(extra) > 0L) {
    fmt <- rbind(fmt, data.table::data.table(field = extra, column = "-", unit = "-"))
  }
  out <- fmt[match(allowed, field)]
  data.table::setindex(out, NULL)
  out[]
}

# ---- reading ----------------------------------------------------------------

read_raw_file <- function(f, id_specs, sheet = 1, ...) {
  ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(f))
  if (ext %in% c("xlsx", "xls")) {
    if (!requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE)) {
      cli::cli_abort(c("Reading Excel files needs the {.pkg readxl} package.",
                       "i" = "Install it with {.code install.packages(\"readxl\")}, or save the file as CSV."))
    }
    header <- names(readxl::read_excel(f, sheet = sheet, n_max = 0L))
    ids <- spec_columns(id_specs, header)
    types <- rep("guess", length(header))
    types[match(ids, header)] <- "text"
    dt <- data.table::as.data.table(
      readxl::read_excel(f, sheet = sheet, col_types = types, .name_repair = "minimal")
    )
    return(dt)
  }
  header <- names(data.table::fread(f, nrows = 0L, showProgress = FALSE, ...))
  ids <- spec_columns(id_specs, header)
  cc <- if (length(ids) > 0L) list(character = ids) else NULL
  data.table::fread(f, colClasses = cc, showProgress = FALSE, ...)
}

# Resolve one column spec ("Tag|耳标号", "6", "Date,Entry") against the
# column names. Returns the matched names, or NULL if any part is missing.
resolve_spec <- function(spec, header) {
  if (is.na(spec) || spec %in% c("", "-")) return(NULL)
  parts <- trimws(strsplit(spec, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])
  out <- character(length(parts))
  key <- tolower(trimws(header))
  for (i in seq_along(parts)) {
    hit <- NA_character_
    for (alt in trimws(strsplit(parts[i], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]])) {
      if (alt %in% header) {
        hit <- alt
      } else if (tolower(alt) %in% key) {
        hit <- header[match(tolower(alt), key)]
      } else if (grepl("^[0-9]+$", alt) && as.integer(alt) >= 1L &&
                 as.integer(alt) <= length(header)) {
        hit <- header[as.integer(alt)]
      }
      if (!is.na(hit)) break
    }
    if (is.na(hit)) return(NULL)
    out[i] <- hit
  }
  out
}

spec_columns <- function(specs, header) {
  unique(unlist(lapply(specs, resolve_spec, header = header)))
}

check_station <- function(station) {
  if (!is.character(station) || length(station) != 1L ||
      !tolower(station) %in% c("nedap", "fire")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg station} must be {.val nedap} or {.val fire}, not {.val {station}}.")
  }
  tolower(station)
}

format_fits <- function(fmt, header, station) {
  found <- fmt[, !vapply(column, function(s) is.null(resolve_spec(s, header)), logical(1))]
  ok <- all(station_required(station) %in% fmt$field[found])
  if (station == "nedap") ok <- ok && any(c("duration", "exit_time") %in% fmt$field[found])
  ok
}

detect_station <- function(data) {
  is_nedap <- format_fits(builtin_format("nedap"), names(data), "nedap")
  is_fire <- format_fits(builtin_format("fire"), names(data), "fire")
  if (is_nedap && !is_fire) return("nedap")
  if (is_fire && !is_nedap) return("fire")
  cli::cli_abort(c(
    "Cannot detect the station type from the column names.",
    "i" = "NEDAP export columns: {.val {c('responder', 'location', 'visit_time', 'duration', 'feed_intake', 'weight')}}.",
    "i" = "FIRE export columns: {.val {c('Tag', 'Location', 'Date', 'Entry', 'Exit', 'Ent Wt', 'Ext Wt', 'Consumed', 'Weight')}}.",
    "i" = "Set {.arg station}, and {.arg format} if the columns have other names (see {.fn station_format})."
  ))
}

# ---- mapping to the standard table -----------------------------------------

apply_format <- function(dt, fmt, station, arg = "data") {
  header <- names(dt)
  n <- nrow(dt)
  ff <- format_fields()
  out <- data.table::data.table(.row = seq_len(n))
  missing_req <- character()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(fmt))) {
    fld <- fmt$field[i]
    cols <- resolve_spec(fmt$column[i], header)
    if (is.null(cols)) {
      if (fmt$column[i] != "-" && fld %in% station_required(station)) {
        missing_req <- c(missing_req, paste0(fld, " (", fmt$column[i], ")"))
      }
      next
    }
    type <- ff$type[ff$field == fld]
    val <- switch(type,
      text = trim_text(dt[[cols[1L]]]),
      time = parse_time(dt[, cols, with = FALSE], fmt$unit[i], fld, arg),
      duration = as_number(dt[[cols[1L]]], fld, arg) * if (fmt$unit[i] == "min") 60 else 1,
      mass_g = to_unit(as_number(dt[[cols[1L]]], fld, arg), fmt$unit[i], "g"),
      mass_kg = to_unit(as_number(dt[[cols[1L]]], fld, arg), fmt$unit[i], "kg")
    )
    data.table::set(out, j = fld, value = val)
  }
  if (station == "nedap" && !any(c("duration", "exit_time") %in% names(out))) {
    missing_req <- c(missing_req, "duration or exit_time")
  }
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "{.arg {arg}} has no column for required field(s): {.val {missing_req}}.",
      "i" = "Columns in the file: {.val {header}}.",
      "i" = "Is {.code station = \"{station}\"} correct? For other column names, give a {.arg format} (see {.fn station_format})."
    ))
  }
  out[, .row := NULL]
  std_cols <- c("responder", "location", "entry_time", "exit_time", "duration",
                "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in", "trough_out", "topup")
  for (col in setdiff(std_cols, names(out))) {
    data.table::set(out, j = col, value = if (col %in% c("entry_time", "exit_time")) {
      as.POSIXct(rep(NA_real_, n), origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
    } else if (col %in% c("responder", "location")) {
      rep(NA_character_, n)
    } else {
      rep(NA_real_, n)
    })
  }
  data.table::setcolorder(out, intersect(c(std_cols, "breed"), names(out)))
  out
}

trim_text <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x[!is.na(x) & x == ""] <- NA_character_
  x
}

as_number <- function(x, fld, arg) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(as.numeric(x))
  y <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trimws(as.character(x))))
  bad <- !is.na(x) & trimws(as.character(x)) != "" & is.na(y)
  if (any(bad)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "Field {.field {fld}} in {.arg {arg}} has values that are not numbers: {.val {utils::head(unique(as.character(x[bad])), 3)}}.",
      "i" = "Check the column in the format (see {.fn station_format})."
    ))
  }
  y
}

to_unit <- function(x, unit, target) {
  if (unit %in% c("-", "auto")) {
    pos <- x[!is.na(x) & x > 0]
    unit <- if (unit == "-") target else if (length(pos) > 0L && stats::median(pos) < 1000) "kg" else "g"
  }
  if (unit == target) x else if (unit == "kg") x * 1000 else x / 1000
}

# Times: one column (date-time) or several (date, clock time) joined. The
# result is the clock time stored as UTC, as everywhere in the package.
parse_time <- function(cols, unit, fld, arg) {
  if (ncol(cols) == 1L && inherits(cols[[1L]], "POSIXct")) {
    return(clock_as_utc(cols[[1L]]))
  }
  piece <- function(x, part) {
    if (inherits(x, "POSIXct")) {
      format(x, if (part == 1L) "%Y-%m-%d" else "%H:%M:%S")
    } else if (inherits(x, "Date")) {
      format(x, "%Y-%m-%d")
    } else {
      trimws(as.character(x))
    }
  }
  txt <- if (ncol(cols) == 1L) {
    piece(cols[[1L]], 1L)
  } else {
    do.call(paste, lapply(seq_along(cols), function(k) piece(cols[[k]], k)))
  }
  txt[!is.na(txt) & grepl("(^|\\s)NA(\\s|$)", txt)] <- NA_character_
  out <- if (unit != "-") {
    as.POSIXct(strptime(txt, unit, tz = "UTC"))
  } else {
    tryCatch(
      as.POSIXct(txt, tz = "UTC", tryFormats = c(
        "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS", "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%OS", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M",
        "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M", "%Y-%m-%d", "%Y/%m/%d")),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  }
  bad <- if (is.null(out)) !is.na(txt) else !is.na(txt) & is.na(out)
  if (any(bad)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "Field {.field {fld}} in {.arg {arg}}: cannot read {sum(bad)} value(s) as time, e.g. {.val {utils::head(txt[bad], 2)}}.",
      "i" = "Give the time format as {.field unit} in the station format, e.g. {.val %d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S}."
    ))
  }
  out
}

resolve_files <- function(files, pattern) {
  if (!is.character(files) || length(files) == 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg files} must be file paths or a folder.")
  }
  if (length(files) == 1L && dir.exists(files)) {
    folder <- files
    files <- list.files(folder, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE,
                        ignore.case = TRUE)
    if (length(files) == 0L) {
      cli::cli_abort("No files matching {.val {pattern}} in {.path {folder}}.")
    }
    return(sort(files))
  }
  missing_files <- files[!file.exists(files)]
  if (length(missing_files) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort("File{?s} not found: {.path {missing_files}}.")
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(basename(files))) {
    cli::cli_abort("File names must be unique: {.val {basename(files)[duplicated(basename(files))]}}.")
  }
  files
}
```

```{r example-read_station}
# Write the example data to two CSV files, then read them back
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "fire_export")
dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 101, ], file.path(folder, "fire_101.csv"))
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 102, ], file.path(folder, "fire_102.csv"))

raw <- read_station(folder)
head(raw)
attr(raw, "station")

# The built-in format, written as a template for other exports
station_format("fire", file = file.path(folder, "fire_format.txt"))

unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)

write_split <- function(data, by, folder) {
  dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (v in unique(data[[by]])) {
    data.table::fwrite(data[data[[by]] == v, ], file.path(folder, paste0("part_", v, ".csv")))
  }
  sort(list.files(folder, full.names = TRUE))
}

  files <- write_split(fire, "Location", folder)

  expect_equal(nrow(out), nrow(fire))
  expect_equal(attr(out, "station"), "fire")
  expect_equal(sort(unique(out$source_file)), c("part_101.csv", "part_102.csv"))

                      "duration", "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in",
                      "trough_out", "topup", "source_file"))
  # units: feed and trough in g, weight in kg
  expect_equal(sort(out$feed_intake), sort(fire$Consumed * 1000))
  expect_equal(sort(out$weight), sort(as.numeric(fire$Weight)))

# station_format

A station format says which column of an export holds which standard
field, and in which unit. `station_format()` shows the built-in format of
a station type and writes it as a template file for other exports.

```{r function-station_format}
#' Station Formats: Map Export Columns to Standard Fields
#'
#' @description
#' A station format tells [read_station()] and [prep_visits()] which column
#' of a station export holds which standard field, and in which unit.
#' `station_format()` returns the built-in format of a station type, and
#' optionally writes it as a tab-separated file to use as a template.
#'
#' @param station `"nedap"` or `"fire"`.
#' @param file Optional path. If given, the format is written there as a
#'   tab-separated text file (with explanatory comment lines starting with
#'   `#`), which can be edited and passed to `read_station(format = )`.
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with one row per field: `field`, `column`,
#'   `unit`, `required` and `description`. Invisibly when `file` is given.
#'
#' @section Format file:
#' A tab-separated text file with a header line `field`, `column`, `unit`
#' (the unit column may be left out). Lines starting with `#` and empty
#' lines are ignored. For example, for a FIRE export with Chinese headers:
#'
#' ```
#' field        column      unit
#' responder    耳标号      -
#' location     站号        -
#' entry_time   日期,进站   -
#' exit_time    日期,出站   -
#' trough_in    进站料重    kg
#' trough_out   出站料重    kg
#' feed_intake  采食量      kg
#' weight       体重        kg
#' ```
#'
#' - `column`: the column name, or its position (`6`). Several
#'   alternatives are separated by `|` (`Tag|耳标号`); the first one found
#'   is used. Two columns separated by `,` are joined for a time field:
#'   date and clock time (`Date,Entry`). `-` or empty means the export
#'   does not have the field (only allowed for optional fields).
#' - `unit`: for `weight`, `feed_intake`, `trough_in`, `trough_out` and
#'   `topup`: `kg`, `g` or `auto` (kg if the median is below 1000,
#'   otherwise g). For `duration`: `s` or `min`. For time fields: `-`
#'   (detect `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss` or `YYYY/MM/DD hh:mm:ss`) or a
#'   [strptime()] format such as `%d/%m/%Y %H:%M`.
#'
#' @section Standard fields:
#' | Field | Type | Standard unit | NEDAP | FIRE |
#' |---|---|---|---|---|
#' | `responder` | text | | required | required |
#' | `location` | text | | required | required |
#' | `entry_time` | time | clock time as UTC | required | required |
#' | `exit_time` | time | clock time as UTC | optional | required |
#' | `duration` | number | s | required* | — |
#' | `feed_intake` | number | g | required | required |
#' | `weight` | number | kg | required | required |
#' | `trough_in`, `trough_out` | number | g | — | required |
#' | `topup` | number | g | — | optional |
#' | `breed` | text | | optional | optional |
#'
#' \* NEDAP needs `duration` or `exit_time`. FIRE computes the duration
#' from entry and exit time; an exit before the entry is a midnight
#' crossing (see [prep_visits()]).
#'
#' @seealso [read_station()].
#' @export
station_format <- function(station = c("nedap", "fire"), file = NULL) {
  station <- check_station(station[1L])
  fmt <- builtin_format(station)
  ff <- format_fields()
  fmt[, required := field %in% station_required(station)]
  fmt[ff, description := i.description, on = "field"]
  if (is.null(file)) return(fmt[])
  header <- c(
    paste0("# tidypptsda station format: ", toupper(station)),
    "# One line per field, separated by tabs: field, column, unit.",
    "# column: column name or position; alternatives with |; date,time joined with ,; - if absent.",
    "# unit: kg / g / auto for masses, s / min for duration, - or a strptime format for times.",
    paste0("# Required fields: ", paste(station_required(station), collapse = ", "), ".")
  )
  writeLines(header, file, useBytes = FALSE)
  data.table::fwrite(fmt[, .(field, column, unit)], file, sep = "\t",
                     append = TRUE, col.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)
  ppt_msg("Station format written to {.file {file}}", "success")
  invisible(fmt[])
}
```

```{r example-station_format}
station_format("nedap")
station_format("fire")

# Write a template, edit it, and use it
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
station_format("fire", file = f)
cat(readLines(f), sep = "\n")
unlink(f)
```

  expect_setequal(n$field, station_fields("nedap"))

  suppressMessages(station_format("nedap", file = file))

})
