```{r tests-calc_adfi}
test_that("loess_pop scales the population curve to the pig", {
  curve <- list(coef = c(500, 40, -0.1), range = c(30, 120), n_pigs = 10L, n_days = 500L)
  f <- function(bw) 500 + 40 * bw - 0.1 * bw^2
  expect_equal(pop_predict(curve, c(20, 50, 130)), f(c(30, 50, 120)))   # held at the range ends
  n <- 60
  d <- data.table::data.table(seq_days = 1:n, bw = 30 + 1.2 * (1:n), in_stage = TRUE)
  d[, dfi_check := 1.1 * f(bw)]                 # the pig eats 10% more than the population
  d[c(1:10, 30:40), dfi_check := NA]            # start and a long gap
  d[, state := data.table::fifelse(is.na(dfi_check), NA_character_, "org")]
  out <- impute_dfi_one_pig(d, qc_config(), pop = list(all = curve))
  nrec <- sum(!is.na(d$dfi_check))
  r <- nrec / (nrec + 10) * 1.1 + 10 / (nrec + 10)
  expect_equal(out$dfi[c(1:10, 30:40)], r * f(d$bw[c(1:10, 30:40)]))
  expect_true(all(out$state[1:10] == "elrp"))
  expect_true(all(out$state[30:40] == "iii"))
  # the curve of the pig's group is used
  d[, pop_key := "breed A"]
  half <- list(coef = curve$coef / 2, range = curve$range)
  out2 <- impute_dfi_one_pig(d, qc_config(), pop = list(all = curve, "breed A" = half))
  expect_equal(out2$dfi[1:10], (nrec / (nrec + 10) * 2.2 + 10 / (nrec + 10)) * f(d$bw[1:10]) / 2)
})

test_that("loess_pop uses the pig's own regression after the last record", {
  curve <- list(coef = c(500, 40, -0.1), range = c(30, 120), n_pigs = 10L, n_days = 500L)
  n <- 60
  d <- data.table::data.table(seq_days = 1:n, bw = 30 + 1.2 * (1:n), in_stage = TRUE)
  d[, dfi_check := 800 + 25 * bw]
  d[c(1:5, 51:60), dfi_check := NA]             # start and end
  d[, state := data.table::fifelse(is.na(dfi_check), NA_character_, "org")]
  out <- impute_dfi_one_pig(d, qc_config(), pop = list(all = curve))
  fit <- stats::lm(dfi_check ~ bw, data = d[!is.na(dfi_check)])
  expect_equal(out$dfi[51:60], unname(stats::predict(fit, newdata = d[51:60])))
  expect_false(isTRUE(all.equal(out$dfi[1:5], unname(stats::predict(fit, newdata = d[1:5])))))
  expect_true(all(out$state[c(1:5, 51:60)] == "elrp"))
})

test_that("calc_adfi fits population curves for all pigs and per breed", {
  r <- run_adfi(nedap)
  pc <- r$adfi$pop_curve
  expect_equal(pc$group, "all")
  expect_gt(pc$n_pigs, 20)
  expect_true(all(c("b0", "b1", "b2", "bw_min", "bw_max") %in% names(pc)))
  expect_false("pop_key" %in% names(r$adfi$daily))
  # per breed: two breeds of 15 pigs each

  # other methods: no curve
  fl <- calc_adfi(r$visits, r$adg, qc = qc_set(r$adg$settings, list(impute_method = "loess_lm")), verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(nrow(fl$pop_curve), 0L)
  # a late entry: the days before the first record differ between the methods
  v <- r$visits
  pig <- r$adg$per_pig[adg_type == "observed", responder][1L]
  start <- r$adg$per_pig[responder == pig, start_date]
  v <- v[!(responder %in% pig & date < start + 20)]
  a <- calc_adg(clean_weight(v, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  pop <- calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0)$per_pig[responder == pig, adfi]
  lm <- calc_adfi(v, a, qc = qc_set(a$settings, list(impute_method = "loess_lm")), verbose = 0)$per_pig[responder == pig, adfi]
  expect_false(isTRUE(all.equal(pop, lm)))
})
```

# calc_fcr

`calc_fcr()` combines ADG and ADFI, both computed over the same body weight
stage, into the feed conversion ratio FCR = ADFI / ADG (kg feed per kg
gain) and its inverse, feed efficiency G:F = ADG / ADFI.

Each pig gets `fcr_flag = "ok"` or `"low_confidence"`, with the reasons in
`fcr_note`: the growth curve or the feed intake extrapolated over more
than `max_edge_extrap_days` (default 15) at the start or end of the stage,
an inner 10 kg class with recorded weights spanning less than
`min_bin_coverage_kg` (default 6 kg), a segment FCR outside the optional
`bin_fcr_limits`,
ADG on part of the stage only, less than `min_coverage` (default 0.7) of
the stage with recorded feed intake, or weight data flagged by
[clean_weight()].

```{r function-calc_fcr}
#' Compute Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR) with Confidence Flags
#'
#' @description
#' Compute feed conversion ratio (FCR) from ADG and ADFI over the same body
#' weight stage, flag pigs whose values rely on extrapolation, and summarise
#' the traits.
#'
#' @param adg Result of [calc_adg()].
#' @param adfi Result of [calc_adfi()] computed from the same `adg`.
#' @param min_coverage Minimum share of stage days with recorded feed
#'   intake for `fcr_flag = "ok"`. Default: `min_coverage` of the QC
#'   settings (0.7).
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).
#'
#' @return An object of class `ppt_fcr` (a list):
#'   - `per_pig`: `adg` (g/d), `adfi` (g/d), `fcr`, `gf`, `adg_type`,
#'     `coverage`, `stage_days`, `start_weight`, `end_weight`, `fcr_flag`,
#'     `fcr_note`;
#'   - `daily`: the daily table of [calc_adfi()];
#'   - `summary`: numeric summary (`n`, `min`, `max`, `median`, `mean`,
#'     `sd`, `cv`) of the main traits, for all pigs, for pigs with
#'     `fcr_flag = "ok"` and, with a `breed` column, for each breed;
#'   - `by_bin`: one row per pig and body weight class of `bin_width` kg
#'     (days are put into classes by the growth curve): feed (`feed_kg`),
#'     gain (`gain_kg`, from the growth curve), segment `fcr`,
#'     `weight_coverage_kg` (span of recorded body weights in the class),
#'     `low_coverage` (inner class covered by less than
#'     `min_bin_coverage_kg`) and `fcr_out` (segment FCR outside
#'     `bin_fcr_limits`);
#'   - `removed`, `settings`.
#'
#' @details
#' FCR = ADFI / ADG, with ADG the slope of the daily weights over the stage
#' (observed, interpolated and curve-filled days, see [calc_adg()]) and ADFI
#' the mean daily intake over the same days (recorded, corrected and
#' imputed, see [calc_adfi()]).
#'
#' @seealso [calc_adg()], [calc_adfi()].
#' @export
calc_fcr <- function(adg, adfi, min_coverage = adg$settings$min_coverage,
                     verbose = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  if (!inherits(adg, "ppt_adg")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg adg} must be the result of {.fn calc_adg}.")
  }
  if (!inherits(adfi, "ppt_adfi")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg adfi} must be the result of {.fn calc_adfi}.")
  }
  if (!identical(adg$settings$stage_range, adfi$settings$stage_range)) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg adg} and {.arg adfi} use different {.field stage_range}.")
  }
  ppt_msg("FCR over {adg$settings$stage_range[1]}-{adg$settings$stage_range[2]} kg", "h1")

  a <- adg$per_pig[, intersect(c("responder", "location", "breed", "stage", "adg", "adg_type",
                                "stage_days", "start_weight", "end_weight", "weight_status",
                                "extrap_days_start", "extrap_days_end"), names(adg$per_pig)),
                   with = FALSE]
  f <- adfi$per_pig[, .(responder, adfi, coverage, n_extrap_start, n_extrap_end)]
  max_edge <- adg$settings$max_edge_extrap_days
  per_pig <- merge(a, f, by = "responder", all.x = TRUE)
  per_pig[, `:=`(fcr = adfi / adg, gf = adg / adfi)]

  notes <- character(nrow(per_pig))
  add_note <- function(cond, text) {
    cond <- cond %in% TRUE
    if (!any(cond)) return(invisible(NULL))
    text <- if (length(text) == 1L) rep(text, sum(cond)) else text[cond]
    notes[cond] <<- ifelse(nzchar(notes[cond]), paste(notes[cond], text, sep = "; "), text)
  }
  add_note(per_pig$adg_type == "partial", "ADG on part of the stage")
  add_note(per_pig$extrap_days_start > max_edge,
           sprintf("growth curve extrapolated %.0f d before the first weight", per_pig$extrap_days_start))
  add_note(per_pig$extrap_days_end > max_edge,
           sprintf("growth curve extrapolated %.0f d after the last weight", per_pig$extrap_days_end))
  add_note(per_pig$n_extrap_start > max_edge,
           sprintf("feed intake extrapolated for the first %d stage days", as.integer(per_pig$n_extrap_start)))
  add_note(per_pig$n_extrap_end > max_edge,
           sprintf("feed intake extrapolated for the last %d stage days", as.integer(per_pig$n_extrap_end)))
  add_note(per_pig$coverage < min_coverage,
           sprintf("feed intake recorded on %.0f%% of the stage", 100 * per_pig$coverage))
  add_note(per_pig$weight_status == "low_confidence", "weight data flagged")
  by_bin <- fcr_by_bin(adg, adfi, adg$settings)
  bin_notes <- by_bin[low_coverage == TRUE | fcr_out == TRUE, .(note = paste(
    c(if (any(low_coverage)) sprintf("weight records cover %.1f kg of %s-%s kg",
                                     weight_coverage_kg[low_coverage], weight_from[low_coverage], weight_to[low_coverage]),
      if (any(fcr_out)) sprintf("segment FCR %.2f outside %s-%s in %s-%s kg", fcr[fcr_out],
                                fcr_min[fcr_out], fcr_max[fcr_out], weight_from[fcr_out], weight_to[fcr_out])),
    collapse = "; ")), by = responder]
  m <- match(per_pig$responder, bin_notes$responder)
  add_note(!is.na(m), bin_notes$note[m])
  add_note(is.na(per_pig$fcr), "no FCR")
  per_pig[, `:=`(fcr_note = notes,
                 fcr_flag = data.table::fifelse(nzchar(notes), "low_confidence", "ok"))]
  per_pig[is.na(fcr), fcr_flag := NA_character_]
  per_pig[, weight_status := NULL]
  data.table::setcolorder(per_pig, intersect(c("responder", "location", "breed", "stage", "adg", "adfi",
                                     "fcr", "gf", "adg_type", "coverage", "stage_days",
                                     "start_weight", "end_weight", "fcr_flag", "fcr_note"), names(per_pig)))
  data.table::setorder(per_pig, location, responder)

  summary <- rbind(
    trait_summary(per_pig, "all"),
    trait_summary(per_pig[fcr_flag %in% "ok"], "ok")
  )
  if ("breed" %in% names(per_pig)) {
    for (b in sort(unique(stats::na.omit(per_pig$breed)))) {
      summary <- rbind(summary, trait_summary(per_pig[breed %in% b], paste("breed", b)))
    }
  }

  n_ok <- per_pig[fcr_flag %in% "ok", .N]
  n_low <- per_pig[fcr_flag %in% "low_confidence", .N]
  ppt_msg("FCR for {sum(!is.na(per_pig$fcr))} pig{?s}: {n_ok} ok, {n_low} low confidence", "info")
  s <- summary[group == "all" & trait == "fcr"]
  if (nrow(s) == 1L && s$n > 0) {
    ppt_msg("Mean FCR {sprintf('%.2f', s$mean)} (SD {sprintf('%.2f', s$sd)}), ADG {round(summary[group == 'all' & trait == 'adg', mean])} g/d, ADFI {round(summary[group == 'all' & trait == 'adfi', mean])} g/d", "success")
  }
  if (n_low > 0L) {
    why <- sort(table(unlist(strsplit(per_pig[fcr_flag %in% "low_confidence", fcr_note], "; "))), decreasing = TRUE)
    why <- unique(gsub("[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?", "N", names(why)))
    ppt_msg("Low confidence because of: {paste(unique(why), collapse = ', ')}", "info", level = 2L)
  }

  new_ppt_result(per_pig = per_pig, daily = adfi$daily, removed = adfi$removed,
                 settings = adg$settings, class = "ppt_fcr") |>
    add_element(summary = summary, by_bin = by_bin)
}

# Feed intake, gain and FCR per body weight class of each pig.
fcr_by_bin <- function(adg, adfi, qc) {
  lo <- qc$stage_range[1L]
  hi <- qc$stage_range[2L]
  width <- qc$bin_width
  cls <- function(w) lo + floor((w - lo) / width) * width
  # Days are put into weight classes by the growth curve, not by the daily
  # weights: the daily weights are noisy, so near a class limit days would
  # fall into the neighbouring class at random and inflate the weight range
  # of the class. The gain of a class is the curve range scaled to its days
  # (daily weights are mid-day values).
  st <- adfi$daily[in_stage == TRUE & !is.na(dfi)]
  st[adg$daily, on = c("responder", "date"), pw := i.predicted]
  st[is.na(pw), pw := bw]
  st <- st[!is.na(pw)]
  st[, weight_from := cls(pw)]
  st <- st[weight_from >= lo & weight_from < hi]
  bins <- st[, .(n_days = .N, n_observed_feed = sum(state %in% c("org", "corr")),
                 feed_kg = sum(dfi) / 1000,
                 gain_kg = if (.N > 1L) (max(pw) - min(pw)) * .N / (.N - 1L) else NA_real_),
             by = .(responder, weight_from)]
  bins[, fcr := feed_kg / gain_kg]
  bins[, weight_to := pmin(weight_from + width, hi)]

  # how much of each class is covered by recorded body weights
  ob <- adg$daily[source == "observed" & !is.na(weight)]
  ob[, weight_from := cls(weight)]
  ob <- ob[weight_from >= lo & weight_from < hi]
  cov <- if (nrow(ob) > 0L) {
    ob[, .(weight_coverage_kg = max(weight) - min(weight)), by = .(responder, weight_from)]
  } else {
    data.table::data.table(responder = character(), weight_from = numeric(),
                           weight_coverage_kg = numeric())
  }
  bins <- merge(bins, cov, by = c("responder", "weight_from"), all.x = TRUE)
  bins[is.na(weight_coverage_kg), weight_coverage_kg := 0]
  rng <- if (nrow(cov) > 0L) {
    cov[, .(first_bin = min(weight_from), last_bin = max(weight_from)), by = responder]
  } else {
    data.table::data.table(responder = character(), first_bin = numeric(), last_bin = numeric())
  }
  bins <- merge(bins, rng, by = "responder", all.x = TRUE)
  bins[, inner := (weight_from > first_bin & weight_from < last_bin) %in% TRUE]
  bins[, low_coverage := inner & weight_coverage_kg < qc$min_bin_coverage_kg]

  bins[, `:=`(fcr_min = NA_real_, fcr_max = NA_real_)]
  if (!is.null(qc$bin_fcr_limits)) {
    lim <- data.table::as.data.table(qc$bin_fcr_limits)
    bins[lim, on = "weight_from", `:=`(fcr_min = i.fcr_min, fcr_max = i.fcr_max)]
  }
  bins[, fcr_out := !is.na(fcr) & !is.na(fcr_min) & (fcr < fcr_min | fcr > fcr_max)]
  bins[, c("first_bin", "last_bin") := NULL]
  data.table::setcolorder(bins, c("responder", "weight_from", "weight_to", "n_days",
                                  "n_observed_feed", "feed_kg", "gain_kg", "fcr",
                                  "weight_coverage_kg", "inner", "low_coverage",
                                  "fcr_min", "fcr_max", "fcr_out"))
  data.table::setorder(bins, responder, weight_from)
  bins[]
}

trait_summary <- function(p, group) {
  traits <- c("adg", "adfi", "fcr", "gf", "stage_days", "start_weight", "end_weight")
  out <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(traits, function(tr) {
    x <- p[[tr]]
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
    n <- length(x)
    data.table::data.table(
      group = group, trait = tr, n = n,
      min = if (n) min(x) else NA_real_,
      max = if (n) max(x) else NA_real_,
      median = if (n) stats::median(x) else NA_real_,
      mean = if (n) mean(x) else NA_real_,
      sd = if (n > 1L) stats::sd(x) else NA_real_
    )
  }))
  out[, cv := sd / mean]
  out[]
}
```

```{r example-calc_fcr}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
adg <- calc_adg(clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg, verbose = 0)
fcr <- calc_fcr(adg, adfi)
head(fcr$per_pig[, .(responder, adg, adfi, fcr, fcr_flag, fcr_note)])
fcr$summary[group == "all"]
```

```{r tests-calc_fcr}
fcr_pipeline <- function(data) {
  v <- prep_visits(data, verbose = 0)
  a <- suppressWarnings(calc_adg(clean_weight(v, verbose = 0), verbose = 0))
  f <- calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0)
  list(adg = a, adfi = f, fcr = calc_fcr(a, f, verbose = 0))
}

test_that("FCR is ADFI / ADG and flags explain themselves", {
  for (data in list(nedap, fire)) {
    r <- fcr_pipeline(data)
    p <- r$fcr$per_pig
    expect_s3_class(r$fcr, c("ppt_fcr", "ppt_result"))
    expect_equal(nrow(p), nrow(r$adg$per_pig))
    expect_equal(p$fcr, p$adfi / p$adg)
    expect_equal(p$gf, 1 / p$fcr)
    ok <- p[!is.na(fcr)]
    expect_true(all(ok$fcr > 1.5 & ok$fcr < 4.5))
    expect_true(all(ok[fcr_flag == "ok", nchar(fcr_note)] == 0))
    expect_true(all(ok[fcr_flag == "low_confidence", nchar(fcr_note)] > 0))
    long <- p[extrap_days_start > 15 | extrap_days_end > 15 | n_extrap_start > 15 | n_extrap_end > 15]
    expect_true(all(long$fcr_flag == "low_confidence"))
    short <- p[!responder %in% long$responder]
    expect_false(any(grepl("extrapolated", short$fcr_note)))
  }
})

test_that("each note describes its own pig", {
  r <- fcr_pipeline(fire)
  p <- r$fcr$per_pig[grepl("feed intake recorded on", fcr_note)]
  expect_gt(nrow(p), 0)
  shown <- as.numeric(sub(".*feed intake recorded on ([0-9]+)%.*", "\\1", p$fcr_note))
  expect_equal(shown, round(100 * p$coverage))
  e <- r$fcr$per_pig[grepl("extrapolated .* d before", fcr_note)]
  shown_d <- as.numeric(sub(".*extrapolated ([0-9]+) d before.*", "\\1", e$fcr_note))
  expect_equal(shown_d, round(e$extrap_days_start))
})

test_that("summary is numeric and consistent", {
  r <- fcr_pipeline(nedap)
  s <- r$fcr$summary
  expect_true(all(vapply(s[, .(n, min, max, median, mean, sd, cv)], is.numeric, logical(1))))
  expect_equal(s[group == "all" & trait == "fcr", mean], mean(r$fcr$per_pig$fcr, na.rm = TRUE))
  expect_equal(s[group == "ok" & trait == "fcr", n], r$fcr$per_pig[fcr_flag %in% "ok", .N])
  expect_equal(s$cv, s$sd / s$mean)
})

test_that("breed enters the correction model and the summary", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  pigs <- unique(v[identified == TRUE, responder])
  v <- add_breed(v, data.frame(responder = pigs, breed = rep(c("YY", "LL"), length.out = length(pigs))), verbose = 0)
  a <- calc_adg(clean_weight(v, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  f <- calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0)
  expect_true(any(grepl("^breed", f$model$term)))
  expect_true("breed" %in% names(f$per_pig))
  r <- calc_fcr(a, f, verbose = 0)
  expect_true(all(c("breed LL", "breed YY") %in% r$summary$group))
  expect_true("breed" %in% names(r$per_pig))
})

test_that("weight classes: coverage and optional FCR limits", {
  r <- fcr_pipeline(nedap)
  b <- r$fcr$by_bin
  expect_true(all(c("weight_from", "weight_to", "feed_kg", "gain_kg", "fcr",
                    "weight_coverage_kg", "low_coverage", "fcr_out") %in% names(b)))
  expect_true(all(b$weight_from >= 30 & b$weight_to <= 120))
  expect_false(any(b$fcr_out))                         # no limits by default
  low <- b[low_coverage == TRUE, unique(responder)]
  expect_true(all(r$fcr$per_pig[responder %in% low, fcr_flag] == "low_confidence"))
  expect_true(all(grepl("weight records cover", r$fcr$per_pig[responder %in% low, fcr_note])))
  # very narrow limits flag every pig
  q <- qc_config(bin_fcr_limits = data.frame(weight_from = seq(30, 110, 10), fcr_min = 2.40, fcr_max = 2.41))
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  a <- calc_adg(clean_weight(v, q, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  f2 <- calc_fcr(a, calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  expect_true(any(f2$by_bin$fcr_out))
  expect_true(all(grepl("segment FCR", f2$per_pig[responder %in% f2$by_bin[fcr_out == TRUE, responder], fcr_note])))
})

test_that("max_edge_extrap_days changes the flags", {
  v <- prep_visits(fire, verbose = 0)
  q <- qc_config(max_edge_extrap_days = 1000, min_coverage = 0)
  a <- suppressWarnings(calc_adg(clean_weight(v, q, verbose = 0), verbose = 0))
  p <- calc_fcr(a, calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)$per_pig
  expect_false(any(grepl("extrapolated", p$fcr_note)))
})

test_that("a stage outside the data gives no R warnings", {
  q <- qc_config(stage_range = c(150, 160), weight_range = c(10, 200))
  expect_no_warning(r <- run_pipeline(nedap, qc = q, verbose = 0))
  expect_true(all(r$fcr$by_bin$weight_coverage_kg == 0))
})

test_that("feed of the adaptation days counts only inside the stage", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  a <- calc_adg(clean_weight(v, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  f <- calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0)
  first <- v[identified == TRUE, .(first = min(date)), by = responder]
  dd <- f$daily[first, on = "responder"][date >= first & date < first + 7]
  # NEDAP pigs enter below 30 kg: their adaptation days are not stage days
  expect_true(all(!dd$in_stage | dd$bw >= 29))
  # a 30-120 kg stage for pigs that enter at ~45 kg starts before entry, so
  # the recorded intake of the adaptation days is part of the stage
  vf <- prep_visits(fire, verbose = 0)
  af <- calc_adg(clean_weight(vf, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  ff <- calc_adfi(vf, af, verbose = 0)
  firstf <- vf[identified == TRUE, .(first = min(date)), by = responder]
  ddf <- ff$daily[firstf, on = "responder"][date >= first & date < first + 7 & in_stage == TRUE]
  expect_gt(nrow(ddf), 0L)
  # every recorded adaptation day inside the stage is used as recorded
  expect_true(all(ddf[!is.na(dfi_raw), state] %in% c("org", "corr")))
})

test_that("min_coverage changes the flags", {
  r <- fcr_pipeline(fire)
  strict <- calc_fcr(r$adg, r$adfi, min_coverage = 1, verbose = 0)$per_pig
  expect_true(all(strict$fcr_flag == "low_confidence"))
})

test_that("inputs are checked and not modified", {
  r <- fcr_pipeline(nedap)
  before <- data.table::copy(r$adg$per_pig)
  calc_fcr(r$adg, r$adfi, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(r$adg$per_pig, before)
  expect_error(calc_fcr(r$adfi, r$adfi), "calc_adg")
  expect_error(calc_fcr(r$adg, r$adg), "calc_adfi")
  other <- r$adfi
  other$settings <- qc_config(stage_range = c(40, 110))
  expect_error(calc_fcr(r$adg, other), "stage_range")
})

test_that("the gain of a weight class is not inflated by daily noise", {
  r <- run_pipeline(nedap, verbose = 0)
  b <- r$fcr$by_bin[inner == TRUE]
  b[r$fcr$per_pig, on = "responder", adg := i.adg]
  # whole days: the gain of a class is within one day of growth of 10 kg
  expect_true(all(abs(b$gain_kg - 10) <= b$adg / 1000 + 0.2))
})
```

# plot_adg, plot_adfi and save_plots

One plot per station, one panel per pig. Axes adapt to the data and to
`stage_range`, so no point is dropped. Colours come from a colour-blind safe
palette (Okabe-Ito) without extra packages.

```{r function-plots}
#' Plot Growth Curves per Station
#'
#' @description
#' Plot the daily body weights, the fitted growth curve and the ADG
#' regression line of each pig, one plot per station. Point colours show
#' where each daily weight comes from: observed (daily median), linear
#' interpolation between recorded days, or the growth curve before the
#' first / after the last recorded day. The straight line over the stage is
#' the regression whose slope is the ADG.
#'
#' @param adg Result of [calc_adg()].
#' @param weight Optional result of [clean_weight()] to also show every
#'   weight record, with outliers highlighted.
#' @param responders,locations Optional pig IDs and stations to plot.
#' @param ncol Number of panel columns. Default 3.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default).
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with one row per station: `location`, `n_pigs`
#'   and `plot` (a list of ggplot objects). Use [save_plots()] to write them
#'   to files.
#' @export
plot_adg <- function(adg, weight = NULL, responders = NULL, locations = NULL,
                     ncol = 3, verbose = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  if (!inherits(adg, "ppt_adg")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg adg} must be the result of {.fn calc_adg}.")
  }
  if (!is.null(weight) && !inherits(weight, "ppt_weight")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg weight} must be the result of {.fn clean_weight}.")
  }
  daily <- filter_pigs(adg$daily, responders, locations)
  info <- adg$per_pig[responder %in% daily$responder]
  stage_rng <- adg$settings$stage_range
  rec <- if (!is.null(weight)) weight$records[responder %in% daily$responder] else NULL

  cols <- c(record = "#BBBBBB", outlier = "#666666", observed = "#0072B2",
            interpolated = "#E69F00", filled = "#CC79A7", curve = "#009E73",
            slope = "#000000", stage = "#000000")
  info[, label := sprintf("ADG %s g/d (R2 %s, %s)\n%s-%s kg in %s d",
                          ifelse(is.na(adg), "NA", format(round(adg))),
                          ifelse(is.na(r_squared), "NA", sprintf("%.3f", r_squared)), adg_type,
                          stage_rng[1L], stage_rng[2L],
                          ifelse(is.na(stage_days), "NA", sprintf("%.1f", stage_days)))]

  # Each plot is built by a top-level helper that only receives its own
  # station's data. A ggplot keeps the environment it was created in, so
  # building it inside this function would drag every pig's records along
  # (hundreds of MB per plot), which makes saving and parallel export slow.
  plots <- lapply(split(daily, by = "location", sorted = TRUE), function(d) {
    lv <- natural_order(unique(d$responder))
    lab <- info[location == d$location[1L] | responder %in% lv]
    r <- if (!is.null(rec)) rec[responder %in% lv] else NULL
    adg_station_plot(d, r, lab, lv, stage_rng, cols, ncol)
  })
  out <- data.table::data.table(location = names(plots),
                                n_pigs = vapply(plots, function(p) data.table::uniqueN(p$data$responder), integer(1)),
                                plot = unname(plots))
  ppt_msg("Created {nrow(out)} growth plot{?s}", "success")
  out
}

#' Plot Daily Feed Intake per Station
#'
#' @description
#' Plot recorded and corrected daily feed intake of each pig over the stage,
#' one plot per station. Point colours show how each day was obtained.
#'
#' @param adfi Result of [calc_adfi()].
#' @inheritParams plot_adg
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with `location`, `n_pigs` and `plot`.
#' @export
plot_adfi <- function(adfi, responders = NULL, locations = NULL, ncol = 3,
                      verbose = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  if (!inherits(adfi, "ppt_adfi")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg adfi} must be the result of {.fn calc_adfi}.")
  }
  daily <- filter_pigs(adfi$daily[in_stage == TRUE], responders, locations)
  info <- adfi$per_pig[responder %in% daily$responder]
  info[, label := sprintf("ADFI %s g/d\nrecorded on %s of the stage",
                          ifelse(is.na(adfi), "NA", format(round(adfi))),
                          ifelse(is.na(coverage), "NA", sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * coverage)))]
  cols <- c(raw = "#BBBBBB", org = "#0072B2", corr = "#E69F00",
            iii = "#009E73", elrp = "#CC79A7", missing = "#D55E00")
  labels <- c(raw = "recorded", org = "error-free", corr = "corrected",
              iii = "filled (between records)", elrp = "filled (stage ends)", missing = "missing")

  plots <- lapply(split(daily, by = "location", sorted = TRUE), function(d) {
    lv <- natural_order(unique(d$responder))
    adfi_station_plot(d, info[responder %in% lv], lv, cols, labels, ncol)
  })
  out <- data.table::data.table(location = names(plots),
                                n_pigs = vapply(plots, function(p) data.table::uniqueN(p$data$responder), integer(1)),
                                plot = unname(plots))
  ppt_msg("Created {nrow(out)} feed intake plot{?s}", "success")
  out
}

#' Save Plots to Files
#'
#' @param plots Result of [plot_adg()] or [plot_adfi()].
#' @param path Folder to write to (created if needed).
#' @param prefix,suffix File name parts: `<prefix>_<location>_<suffix>.<device>`.
#' @param device `"png"`, `"pdf"`, `"jpeg"` or `"tiff"`.
#' @param dpi Resolution for bitmap devices. Default 300.
#' @param width,height Size in cm. By default computed from the number of
#'   panels.
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores: stations are saved in parallel when
#'   > 1. Default 1. Saving is mostly ggplot2 drawing time (about 1 s per
#'   station of 15 pigs), so with many stations this is the main speed-up.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default).
#'
#' @return Invisibly, a `data.table` with `location`, `file` and `saved`.
#' @export
save_plots <- function(plots, path, prefix = "station", suffix = "plot",
                       device = c("png", "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff"), dpi = 300,
                       width = NULL, height = NULL, verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  device <- match.arg(device)
  cores <- check_cores(cores)
  if (!data.table::is.data.table(plots) || !all(c("location", "plot") %in% names(plots))) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg plots} must be the result of {.fn plot_adg} or {.fn plot_adfi}.")
  }
  dir.create(path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  n <- nrow(plots)
  jobs <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    p <- plots$plot[[i]]
    nc <- p$facet$params$ncol %||% 3L
    list(plot = p,
         file = file.path(path, paste0(prefix, "_", plots$location[i], "_", suffix, ".", device)),
         width = width %||% max(16, 9 * nc),
         height = height %||% (6 * ceiling(plots$n_pigs[i] / nc) + 4))
  })

  errs <- run_with_progress(jobs, save_one_plot, cores = min(cores, n),
                            label = "Saving plots", device = device, dpi = dpi)

  files <- vapply(jobs, `[[`, "", "file")
  ok <- vapply(errs, function(e) is.character(e) && length(e) == 1L && is.na(e), logical(1))
  for (i in which(!ok)) {
    msg <- if (is.character(errs[[i]])) errs[[i]] else "worker failed"
    file <- files[i]
    ppt_warn("Could not save {.file {file}}: {msg}")
  }
  res <- data.table::data.table(location = plots$location, file = files, saved = ok)
  ppt_msg("Saved {sum(res$saved)} of {nrow(res)} plot{?s} to {.path {path}}",
          if (all(res$saved)) "success" else "warning")
  invisible(res)
}

# Save one plot; returns NA on success or the error message.
save_one_plot <- function(job, device, dpi) {
  tryCatch({
    ggplot2::ggsave(job$file, job$plot, width = job$width, height = job$height,
                    units = "cm", dpi = dpi, device = device, limitsize = FALSE)
    NA_character_
  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
}

adg_station_plot <- function(d, rec, lab, lv, stage_rng, cols, ncol) {
  loc <- d$location[1L]
  d <- data.table::copy(d)[, responder := factor(responder, levels = lv)]
  lab <- data.table::copy(lab)[, responder := factor(responder, levels = lv)]
  lab <- lab[!is.na(responder)]
  d[, kind := data.table::fifelse(source == "curve", "filled", source)]
  y_rng <- range(c(d$lower, d$upper, d$weight_filled, stage_rng, rec$weight), na.rm = TRUE)
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x = date)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = stage_rng, linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = cols[["stage"]], alpha = 0.4) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                         fill = cols[["curve"]], alpha = 0.15)
  if (!is.null(rec)) {
    r <- data.table::copy(rec)[, responder := factor(responder, levels = lv)]
    r[, kind := data.table::fifelse(outlier, "outlier", "record")]
    r <- r[, .(date, responder, weight, kind)]
    # outliers as small grey crosses, so that they do not look like filled weights
    p <- p +
      ggplot2::geom_point(data = r[kind == "record"], ggplot2::aes(y = weight, colour = kind),
                          size = 0.4, alpha = 0.6) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(data = r[kind == "outlier"], ggplot2::aes(y = weight, colour = kind),
                          size = 0.7, alpha = 0.6, shape = 4)
  }
  # ADG regression line over the stage days
  sl <- d[in_stage == TRUE & !is.na(weight_filled),
          if (.N >= 7L) {
            f <- stats::lm(weight_filled ~ as.numeric(date))
            data.table::data.table(x = range(date), y = stats::predict(f)[c(which.min(date), which.max(date))])
          }, by = responder]
  brk <- c("observed", "interpolated", "filled", "curve", "slope",
           if (!is.null(rec)) c("record", "outlier"))
  brk <- intersect(brk, c(unique(d$kind), "curve", if (nrow(sl) > 0L) "slope", if (!is.null(rec)) c("record", "outlier")))
  p <- p +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = d[!is.na(weight_filled)],
                        ggplot2::aes(y = weight_filled, colour = kind), size = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = predicted, colour = "curve"), linewidth = 0.6)
  # the ADG line on top of the points
  if (nrow(sl) > 0L) {
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_line(data = sl, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, colour = "slope"),
                                linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "longdash")
  }
  p +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = lab, ggplot2::aes(label = label),
                       x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2,
                       size = 2.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~responder, ncol = min(ncol, length(lv))) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = y_rng + c(-2, 12)) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
      name = NULL, values = cols, breaks = brk,
      labels = c(observed = "daily weight (observed)", interpolated = "daily weight (interpolated)",
                 filled = "daily weight (growth curve)", curve = "growth curve",
                 slope = "ADG regression line", record = "weight record", outlier = "outlier")[brk],
      guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(
        linetype = ifelse(brk %in% c("curve", "slope"), "solid", "blank"),
        shape = ifelse(brk %in% c("curve", "slope"), NA, ifelse(brk == "outlier", 4, 16)),
        size = ifelse(brk %in% c("record", "outlier"), 1, 1.5)))
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = paste("Station", loc), x = NULL, y = "Body weight (kg)") +
    ppt_theme()
}

adfi_station_plot <- function(d, lab, lv, cols, labels, ncol) {
  loc <- d$location[1L]
  d <- data.table::copy(d)[, responder := factor(responder, levels = lv)]
  d <- d[, .(date, responder, dfi, dfi_raw, state)]
  lab <- data.table::copy(lab)[, responder := factor(responder, levels = lv)]
  y_max <- max(c(d$dfi, d$dfi_raw), na.rm = TRUE)
  brk <- intersect(names(cols), c("raw", unique(d$state)))
  ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x = date)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(data = lab, ggplot2::aes(yintercept = adfi),
                        linetype = "dashed", colour = "#666666", alpha = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = d[!is.na(dfi_raw)],
                        ggplot2::aes(y = dfi_raw, colour = "raw"), size = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = d[!is.na(dfi)], ggplot2::aes(y = dfi),
                       colour = "#666666", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = d[!is.na(dfi)],
                        ggplot2::aes(y = dfi, colour = state), size = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = lab, ggplot2::aes(label = label),
                       x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2,
                       size = 2.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~responder, ncol = min(ncol, length(lv))) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(min(0, d$dfi_raw, d$dfi, na.rm = TRUE), y_max * 1.25)) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(name = NULL, values = cols, breaks = brk,
                                 labels = labels[brk]) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = paste("Station", loc), x = NULL,
                  y = "Daily feed intake (g)") +
    ppt_theme()
}

filter_pigs <- function(daily, responders, locations) {
  out <- daily
  if (!is.null(responders)) {
    unknown <- setdiff(as.character(responders), out$responder)
    if (length(unknown) > 0L) ppt_warn("Pig{?s} not found: {.val {unknown}}")
    out <- out[responder %in% as.character(responders)]
  }
  if (!is.null(locations)) {
    unknown <- setdiff(as.character(locations), out$location)
    if (length(unknown) > 0L) ppt_warn("Station{?s} not found: {.val {unknown}}")
    out <- out[location %in% as.character(locations)]
  }
  if (nrow(out) == 0L) cli::cli_abort("No data left to plot after filtering.")
  data.table::copy(out)
}

# Numeric IDs sorted as numbers, other IDs alphabetically.
natural_order <- function(x) {
  x <- unique(as.character(x))
  num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("_.*$", "", x)))
  x[order(is.na(num), num, x)]
}

ppt_theme <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2"),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
    )
}
```

# run_pipeline

`run_pipeline()` runs every step with one set of QC settings and keeps all
intermediate results.

```{r function-run_pipeline}
#' Run the Whole Analysis Pipeline
#'
#' @description
#' Run [prep_visits()], [clean_weight()], [calc_adg()], [calc_adfi()] and
#' [calc_fcr()] in a row with the same QC settings.
#'
#' @param data Raw station data (see [prep_visits()]).
#' @param station `"nedap"`, `"fire"` or `NULL` to detect it.
#' @param qc QC settings from [qc_config()].
#' @param breeds Optional breed table passed to [add_breed()] (columns
#'   `responder` and `breed`).
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores for the per-pig computations. Default 1.
#'
#' @return An object of class `ppt_pipeline`: a list with `visits`,
#'   `weight`, `adg`, `adfi` and `fcr`, plus `removed` (every pig removed,
#'   with the step and the reason).
#' @export
run_pipeline <- function(data, station = NULL, qc = qc_config(), breeds = NULL,
                         verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  check_qc(qc)
  visits <- prep_visits(data, station = station, qc = qc, verbose = verbose)
  if (!is.null(breeds)) visits <- add_breed(visits, breeds, verbose = verbose)
  weight <- clean_weight(visits, qc = qc, verbose = verbose, cores = cores)
  adg <- calc_adg(weight, qc = qc, verbose = verbose, cores = cores)
  adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, adg, qc = qc, verbose = verbose, cores = cores)
  fcr <- calc_fcr(adg, adfi, verbose = verbose)
  structure(
    list(visits = visits, weight = weight, adg = adg, adfi = adfi, fcr = fcr,
         removed = fcr$removed),
    class = "ppt_pipeline"
  )
}

#' @export
print.ppt_pipeline <- function(x, ...) {
  cli::cli_h2("tidypptsda pipeline ({toupper(attr(x$visits, 'station'))})")
  n_id <- data.table::uniqueN(x$visits$responder, na.rm = TRUE)
  p <- x$fcr$per_pig
  cli::cli_bullets(c(
    "*" = "Pigs in the data: {n_id}",
    "*" = "Pigs with weight data kept: {x$weight$per_pig[status != 'removed', .N]}",
    "*" = "Pigs with ADG: {sum(!is.na(x$adg$per_pig$adg))}",
    "*" = "Pigs with FCR: {sum(!is.na(p$fcr))} ({sum(p$fcr_flag %in% 'ok')} ok, {sum(p$fcr_flag %in% 'low_confidence')} low confidence)",
    "*" = "Removed pigs: {data.table::uniqueN(x$removed$responder)} (see {.field $removed})"
  ))
  s <- x$fcr$summary[group == "all" & trait %in% c("adg", "adfi", "fcr")]
  if (nrow(s) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_text("Mean ADG {round(s[trait == 'adg', mean])} g/d, ADFI {round(s[trait == 'adfi', mean])} g/d, FCR {sprintf('%.2f', s[trait == 'fcr', mean])}")
  }
  invisible(x)
}
```

```{r example-run_pipeline}
res
```

```{r tests-run_pipeline}
test_that("every pig is either analysed or listed with a reason", {
  for (data in list(nedap, fire)) {
    for (q in list(qc_config(), qc_config(impute_method = "linear", curve_model = "poly3"))) {
      res <- suppressWarnings(run_pipeline(data, qc = q, verbose = 0))
      expect_s3_class(res, "ppt_pipeline")
      ids <- unique(stats::na.omit(res$visits$responder))
      with_fcr <- res$fcr$per_pig[!is.na(fcr), responder]
      expect_setequal(union(with_fcr, res$removed$responder), ids)

      expect_true(all(res$fcr$per_pig$responder %in% res$adg$per_pig$responder))
    }
  }
})
```
