# write_results

`write_results()` writes the tables of an analysis to CSV files named
`<farm>_<table>_<date>.csv`, ready to send to the testing station. Files
are UTF-8 with a byte order mark so that Excel shows Chinese text correctly.

```{r function-write_results}
#' Write Analysis Results to CSV Files
#'
#' @description
#' Write the result tables of [run_pipeline()] (or of a single step such as
#' [calc_fcr()]) to CSV files.
#'
#' @param x Result of [run_pipeline()], or of [clean_weight()],
#'   [calc_adg()], [calc_adfi()] or [calc_fcr()].
#' @param dir Folder to write to (created if needed). Default: working
#'   directory.
#' @param farm Farm or station code used as file name prefix.
#' @param date Date in the file names. Default: today.
#' @param bom Write a UTF-8 byte order mark (for Excel). Default `TRUE`.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default).
#'
#' @details
#' For a [run_pipeline()] result the files are:
#' - `fcr`: one row per pig with ADG, ADFI, FCR and confidence flags;
#' - `by_bin`: feed, gain and FCR per body weight class;
#' - `daily_feed`: daily feed intake (recorded, corrected, imputed);
#' - `daily_weight`: daily body weight (observed, filled and fitted);
#' - `weight_pigs`: weight checks of every pig;
#' - `feed_model`: coefficients of the feed intake correction model;
#' - `removed`: removed pigs with step and reason;
#' - `settings`: the QC settings used.
#'
#' For a single step, its `per_pig`, `daily` and `removed` tables (and
#' `by_bin`, `model` or `summary` when present) are written.
#'
#' @return Invisibly, a `data.table` with `table`, `file` and `rows`.
#' @export
write_results <- function(x, dir = ".", farm = "farm", date = Sys.Date(),
                          bom = TRUE, verbose = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  if (!is.character(farm) || length(farm) != 1L || !nzchar(farm)) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg farm} must be a single non-empty string.")
  }
  tables <- if (inherits(x, "ppt_pipeline")) {
    list(fcr = x$fcr$per_pig, by_bin = x$fcr$by_bin, daily_feed = x$adfi$daily,
         daily_weight = x$adg$daily, weight_pigs = x$weight$per_pig,
         feed_model = x$adfi$model, summary = x$fcr$summary,
         removed = x$removed, settings = settings_table(x$fcr$settings))
  } else if (inherits(x, "ppt_result")) {
    keep <- intersect(c("per_pig", "daily", "by_bin", "summary", "model", "removed"), names(x))
    c(x[keep], list(settings = settings_table(x$settings)))
  } else {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg x} must be the result of {.fn run_pipeline} or of a {.code calc_*} function.")
  }
  tables <- tables[!vapply(tables, is.null, logical(1))]
  dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  stamp <- format(as.Date(date), "%Y%m%d")
  out <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(names(tables), function(nm) {
    file <- file.path(dir, sprintf("%s_%s_%s.csv", farm, nm, stamp))
    data.table::fwrite(tables[[nm]], file, bom = bom)
    data.table::data.table(table = nm, file = file, rows = nrow(tables[[nm]]))
  }))
  ppt_msg("Wrote {nrow(out)} file{?s} to {.path {dir}}", "success")
  invisible(out)
}

# QC settings as a two-column table.
settings_table <- function(qc) {
  if (is.null(qc)) return(NULL)
  val <- vapply(names(qc), function(nm) {
    v <- qc[[nm]]
    if (is.null(v)) "NULL" else if (is.data.frame(v)) sprintf("table (%d rows)", nrow(v)) else paste(v, collapse = ", ")
  }, character(1))
  data.table::data.table(parameter = names(qc), value = unname(val))
}
```

```{r example-write_results}
res <- run_pipeline(nedap, verbose = 0)
out <- write_results(res, dir = file.path(tempdir(), "results"), farm = "demo")
out
unlink(file.path(tempdir(), "results"), recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r tests-write_results}
test_that("write_results writes every table of a pipeline", {
  res <- run_pipeline(fire, qc = qc_config(stage_range = c(60, 120)), verbose = 0)
  dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
  out <- write_results(res, dir, farm = "A01", date = as.Date("2026-10-21"), verbose = 0)
  expect_true(all(file.exists(out$file)))
  expect_true("A01_fcr_20261021.csv" %in% basename(out$file))
  expect_setequal(out$table, c("fcr", "by_bin", "daily_feed", "daily_weight", "weight_pigs",
                               "feed_model", "summary", "removed", "settings"))
  fcr <- data.table::fread(out[table == "fcr", file])
  expect_equal(nrow(fcr), nrow(res$fcr$per_pig))
  st <- data.table::fread(out[table == "settings", file])
  expect_equal(st[parameter == "stage_range", value], "60, 120")
  # BOM for Excel
  expect_equal(readBin(out$file[1], "raw", 3), as.raw(c(0xef, 0xbb, 0xbf)))
})

test_that("write_results works for a single step and rejects other input", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  w <- clean_weight(v, verbose = 0)
  dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
  out <- write_results(w, dir, farm = "x", verbose = 0)
  expect_setequal(out$table, c("per_pig", "daily", "removed", "settings"))
  expect_error(write_results(list(), dir), "run_pipeline")
  expect_error(write_results(w, dir, farm = ""), "farm")
})
```

# validate_outliers, validate_adg and validate_adfi

Three functions check how well the methods work **on your own data**, by
hiding or spoiling part of the data on purpose and measuring how close the
result comes to what is known:

- `validate_outliers()` adds artificial errors to clean weight records and
  measures how many each outlier method finds, how many good records it
  removes, and how much ADG is affected;
- `validate_adg()` compares growth curve models (and, with `extrap`, the
  curve or tangent extrapolation) by k-fold cross-validation on recorded
  days, and by how much ADG changes when the first or last days of the test
  are hidden (late entry, early exit);
- `validate_weight_fill()` hides recorded daily weights of the stage (random
  days, blocks, start or end), fills them again with each weight fill method
  and compares the filled weights and ADG with the recorded ones;
- `validate_adfi()` hides recorded feed intake days in the same way, imputes
  them again with each method (`"loess_pop"` with leave-one-out population
  curves, `"loess_lm"`, `"linear"`) and compares ADFI with the recorded
  value.

```{r function-validate}
#' Validate Weight Outlier Methods with Artificial Errors
#'
#' @description
#' Add artificial errors to body weight records that passed the checks, then
#' run [clean_weight()] with each outlier method and measure how many
#' artificial errors are found, how many good records are removed, and how
#' far ADG moves from the ADG of the clean records.
#'
#' @param visits Result of [prep_visits()].
#' @param qc QC settings from [qc_config()]. They define the clean records
#'   (records kept by `qc`) and every setting except `weight_outlier`.
#' @param methods Named list of outlier method sets to compare. Each element
#'   holds values of `weight_outlier`, plus `"track"` to track the weight
#'   back from the end of the test first (`weight_track = TRUE`); sets
#'   without `"track"` run without tracking. `"track"` alone is the tracking
#'   without any other method.
#' @param rate Share of clean records that receive an artificial error.
#'   Default 0.05.
#' @param size Range of the error size in kg. Default `c(3, 15)`.
#' @param direction `"both"` (default): errors are added or subtracted at
#'   random; `"down"`: weights too low only (pig partly on the scale);
#'   `"up"`: too high only (two pigs on the scale).
#' @param reps Number of repetitions. Default 3.
#' @param max_pigs Use a random sample of at most this many pigs, to save
#'   time on large data (a few hundred pigs are enough). Default `NULL`: all.
#' @param seed Random seed, for reproducible results.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary and progress, default).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores for [clean_weight()] and [calc_adg()].
#'
#' @details
#' The clean records are those that `qc` keeps, so they are not free of error
#' themselves. A method that disagrees with `qc` therefore gets a higher
#' `false_positive_rate`; compare methods mainly on `sensitivity` and ADG.
#' The row `none` shows the result when only `weight_range` is applied
#' (errors that push a weight outside it are still found).
#'
#' Errors placed at random times shift single records but hardly move a
#' growth curve fitted to hundreds of records, so ADG differences between
#' methods are small; they mostly reflect which good records each method
#' removes.
#'
#' @filename validate
#' @return A list of class `ppt_validation` with
#' - `summary`: one row per method: `sensitivity` (share of artificial errors
#'   found), `false_positive_rate` (share of clean records removed),
#'   `precision`, `adg_bias` and `adg_rmse` (g/d, against the ADG of the
#'   clean records), `adg_spearman` (rank correlation) and `n_pigs`;
#' - `per_rep`: the same for each repetition;
#' - `settings`.
#' @export
validate_outliers <- function(visits, qc = qc_config(),
                              methods = list("track+rlm+loess" = c("track", "rlm", "loess"),
                                             track = "track", rlm = "rlm", loess = "loess",
                                             "rlm+loess" = c("rlm", "loess"),
                                             stl = "stl", sd = "sd"),
                              rate = 0.05, size = c(3, 15),
                              direction = c("both", "down", "up"), reps = 3,
                              max_pigs = NULL, seed = 1, verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  direction <- match.arg(direction)
  check_qc(qc)
  if (!is.list(methods) || is.null(names(methods)) || any(!nzchar(names(methods)))) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg methods} must be a named list of {.field weight_outlier} values.")
  }
  for (m in methods) qc_validate(outlier_qc(qc, m))
  if (!is.numeric(rate) || length(rate) != 1L || rate <= 0 || rate >= 1) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg rate} must be a number between 0 and 1.")
  }
  ppt_msg("Validating weight outlier methods ({reps} repetition{?s}, {round(100 * rate)}% artificial errors)", "h1")

  set.seed(seed)
  ref <- clean_weight(visits, qc, verbose = 0, cores = cores)
  kept <- sample_pigs(ref$per_pig[status != "removed", responder], max_pigs)
  ref$per_pig <- ref$per_pig[responder %in% kept]
  ref$records <- ref$records[responder %in% kept]
  truth <- ref$records[outlier == FALSE & responder %in% kept,
                       .(responder, location, date, seq_days, entry_time, weight)]
  truth[, `:=`(identified = TRUE, key = .I)]
  adg_true <- calc_adg(ref, qc, verbose = 0, cores = cores)$per_pig[, .(responder, adg_true = adg)]

  spoiled <- lapply(seq_len(reps), function(r) {
    d <- data.table::copy(truth)
    hit <- stats::runif(nrow(d)) < rate
    d[, injected := hit]
    sgn <- switch(direction, both = sample(c(-1, 1), sum(hit), TRUE),
                  down = rep(-1, sum(hit)), up = rep(1, sum(hit)))
    d[hit, weight := weight + sgn * stats::runif(sum(hit), size[1L], size[2L])]
    d
  })
  jobs <- c(
    lapply(seq_len(reps), function(r) list(rep = r, method = "none", d = spoiled[[r]])),
    unlist(lapply(seq_len(reps), function(r) lapply(names(methods), function(m)
      list(rep = r, method = m, d = spoiled[[r]]))), recursive = FALSE)
  )
  # jobs run in parallel, so each job fits its pigs on one core
  res <- run_with_progress(jobs, validate_outlier_job, label = "Validating outlier methods",
                           qc = qc, methods = methods, adg_true = adg_true, cores = cores,
                           job_cores = 1L)
  per_rep <- data.table::rbindlist(res)
  per_rep[, method := factor(method, levels = c("none", names(methods)))]
  data.table::setorder(per_rep, method, rep)
  num <- setdiff(names(per_rep), c("method", "rep"))
  summary <- per_rep[, lapply(.SD, mean), by = method, .SDcols = num]
  summary[, method := as.character(method)]
  per_rep[, method := as.character(method)]

  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L) {
    ms <- summary[method != "none"]
    ppt_msg(sprintf("%s: %.0f%% of errors found, %.1f%% of good records removed, ADG error %.1f g/d",
                    ms$method, 100 * ms$sensitivity, 100 * ms$false_positive_rate, ms$adg_rmse),
            "bullets")
  }
  structure(list(summary = summary, per_rep = per_rep,
                 settings = list(qc = qc, methods = methods, rate = rate, size = size,
                                 direction = direction, reps = reps, seed = seed)),
            class = c("ppt_validation", "ppt_result"))
}

# qc with another outlier method set: "track" switches the tracking on,
# the other values are weight_outlier methods ("majority" needs two). The
# tracking alone runs rlm with a cutoff of 0, which flags nothing.
outlier_qc <- function(qc, m) {
  track <- "track" %in% m
  m <- setdiff(m, "track")
  q <- if (length(m) == 0L) {
    qc_set(qc, list(weight_outlier = "rlm", rlm_cutoff = 0, outlier_combine = "any"))
  } else {
    qc_set(qc, list(weight_outlier = m))
  }
  q <- qc_set(q, list(weight_track = track))
  if (q$outlier_combine == "majority" && length(q$weight_outlier) < 2L) {
    q <- qc_set(q, list(outlier_combine = "any"))
  }
  q
}

# One repetition x method of validate_outliers().
validate_outlier_job <- function(job, qc, methods, adg_true, job_cores = 1L) {
  d <- job$d
  q <- if (job$method == "none") qc else outlier_qc(qc, methods[[job$method]])
  # the clean records already start after the adaptation period
  q <- qc_set(q, list(adapt_days = 0))
  w <- clean_weight(d, q, verbose = 0, cores = job_cores)
  if (job$method == "none") {
    w$records[qc_flag != "weight_range", `:=`(outlier = FALSE, qc_flag = "")]
  }
  # identical records get identical flags; unique keys keep one row per record
  flags <- unique(w$records[, .(responder, entry_time, weight, outlier)],
                  by = c("responder", "entry_time", "weight"))
  m <- d[flags, on = c("responder", "entry_time", "weight"), nomatch = NULL]
  a <- calc_adg(w, q, verbose = 0, cores = job_cores)$per_pig[, .(responder, adg)]
  a <- a[adg_true, on = "responder", nomatch = NULL][!is.na(adg) & !is.na(adg_true)]
  tp <- sum(m$injected & m$outlier)
  data.table::data.table(
    method = job$method, rep = job$rep,
    sensitivity = tp / max(1L, sum(m$injected)),
    false_positive_rate = sum(!m$injected & m$outlier) / max(1L, sum(!m$injected)),
    precision = if (sum(m$outlier) > 0L) tp / sum(m$outlier) else NA_real_,
    adg_bias = mean(a$adg - a$adg_true),
    adg_rmse = sqrt(mean((a$adg - a$adg_true)^2)),
    adg_spearman = if (nrow(a) > 2L) stats::cor(a$adg, a$adg_true, method = "spearman") else NA_real_,
    n_pigs = nrow(a)
  )
}

#' Validate Growth Curve Models
#'
#' @description
#' Compare growth curve models on the valid weight records of each pig, in
#' two ways:
#' - **k-fold cross-validation**: the recorded days of each pig are split
#'   into `k` groups; each group in turn is left out, the curve is fitted on
#'   the others and predicts the weights of the left-out days;
#' - **truncation**: the first (late entry) or last (early exit) `trim_days`
#'   days are hidden, ADG is computed again and compared with the ADG from
#'   all records of the same model.
#'
#' @param weight Result of [clean_weight()].
#' @param models Curve models to compare (values of `curve_model`).
#' @param extrap Extrapolations to compare (values of `curve_extrap`):
#'   `"start"`, `"curve"`, `"tangent"` or several. Default: the one of
#'   `qc`. Other than `"curve"`, a model is labelled e.g. `"poly2+tangent"`. Mainly the truncation results differ:
#'   cross-validation differs only for left-out days at the very ends of the
#'   records.
#' @param k Number of folds. Default 5.
#' @param trim_days Days hidden at the start or the end of the test.
#'   Default `c(10, 20)`.
#' @param qc QC settings; `stage_range` and `max_extrap_days` are used.
#' @param max_pigs Use a random sample of at most this many pigs. Default
#'   `NULL`: all.
#' @param seed Random seed for the folds.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary and progress, default).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores. Default 1.
#'
#' @return A list of class `ppt_validation` with
#' - `summary`: one row per model (and extrapolation): `cv_rmse` and `cv_mae` (kg, weight of the
#'   left-out records), and for each truncation (`late10`, `early10`, ...)
#'   the ADG `bias`, `rmse` (g/d) and Spearman rank correlation `spearman`
#'   with the full-data ADG, and how many pigs still get an ADG (`n`);
#' - `cv`: cross-validation error of every pig and model;
#' - `truncation`: ADG of every pig, model and truncation;
#' - `settings`.
#' @export
validate_adg <- function(weight, models = c("poly1", "poly2", "poly3", "gompertz"),
                         extrap = NULL,
                         k = 5, trim_days = c(10, 20), qc = weight$settings,
                         max_pigs = NULL, seed = 1, verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  local_cores(cores)
  if (!inherits(weight, "ppt_weight")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg weight} must be the result of {.fn clean_weight}.")
  }
  check_qc(qc)
  for (m in models) qc_validate(qc_set(qc, list(curve_model = m)))
  extrap <- extrap %||% qc$curve_extrap %||% "curve"
  for (e in extrap) qc_validate(qc_set(qc, list(curve_extrap = e)))
  configs <- curve_configs(models, extrap)
  if (!is.numeric(k) || length(k) != 1L || k < 2) cli::cli_abort("{.arg k} must be at least 2.")
  ppt_msg("Validating growth curves: {k}-fold cross-validation and truncation", "h1")

  set.seed(seed)
  kept <- sample_pigs(weight$per_pig[status != "removed", responder], max_pigs)
  rec <- weight$records[outlier == FALSE & responder %in% kept,
                        .(responder, date, entry_time, weight)]
  data.table::setorder(rec, responder, entry_time)
  rec[, fold := {
    days <- unique(date)
    sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(days)))[match(date, days)]
  }, by = responder]
  day0 <- weight$daily[, min(date - seq_days + 1L)]

  fits <- fit_by_pig(rec, validate_adg_one_pig, step = "validate_adg", qc = qc,
                     configs = configs, trim_days = trim_days, day0 = day0)
  out <- fits$result
  cv <- out[type == "cv", .(responder, model, rmse, mae)]
  tr <- out[type != "cv", .(responder, model, truncation = type, adg, adg_full)]

  cv_sum <- cv[, .(cv_rmse = mean(rmse, na.rm = TRUE), cv_mae = mean(mae, na.rm = TRUE)),
               by = model]
  tr_sum <- tr[!is.na(adg_full), .(
    bias = mean(adg - adg_full, na.rm = TRUE),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((adg - adg_full)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    spearman = if (sum(!is.na(adg)) > 2L) stats::cor(adg, adg_full, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs") else NA_real_,
    n = sum(!is.na(adg))
  ), by = .(model, truncation)]
  wide <- data.table::dcast(tr_sum, model ~ truncation, value.var = c("bias", "rmse", "spearman", "n"),
                            sep = "_")
  summary <- merge(cv_sum, wide, by = "model", all = TRUE)
  ord <- unlist(lapply(unique(tr$truncation), function(t) paste0(c("bias_", "rmse_", "spearman_", "n_"), t)))
  data.table::setcolorder(summary, c("model", "cv_rmse", "cv_mae", intersect(ord, names(summary))))
  summary <- summary[match(configs$label, model)]

  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L && nrow(summary) > 0L) {
    best <- summary[which.min(cv_rmse)]
    ppt_msg("Lowest cross-validation error: {.val {best$model}} ({round(best$cv_rmse, 2)} kg)", "success")
  }
  structure(list(summary = summary, cv = cv, truncation = tr, failed = fits$failed,
                 settings = list(qc = qc, models = models, extrap = extrap, k = k,
                                 trim_days = trim_days, seed = seed)),
            class = c("ppt_validation", "ppt_result"))
}

# Model x extrapolation combinations to compare, with their labels.
curve_configs <- function(models, extrap) {
  cfg <- data.table::CJ(model = models, extrap = extrap, sorted = FALSE)
  cfg[, label := data.table::fifelse(extrap == "curve", model, paste0(model, "+", extrap))]
  cfg[]
}

# Cross-validation and truncation of one pig for validate_adg().
validate_adg_one_pig <- function(d, qc, configs, trim_days, day0) {
  first_day <- min(d$date)
  t <- as.numeric(difftime(d$entry_time, as.POSIXct(first_day, tz = "UTC"), units = "days"))
  y <- d$weight
  folds <- sort(unique(d$fold))
  rows <- list()
  for (ci in seq_len(nrow(configs))) {
    m <- configs$model[ci]
    ex <- configs$extrap[ci]
    lab <- configs$label[ci]
    # cross-validation: weight of the left-out days
    err <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
    for (f in folds) {
      test <- d$fold == f
      if (sum(!test) < 10L) next
      curve <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(fit_growth_curve(t[!test], y[!test], m, ex)),
                        error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(curve)) err[test] <- y[test] - curve$pred(t[test])
    }
    rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
      type = "cv", model = lab, rmse = sqrt(mean(err^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
      mae = mean(abs(err), na.rm = TRUE), adg = NA_real_, adg_full = NA_real_)
    # truncation: ADG with the first / last days hidden
    q <- qc_set(qc, list(curve_model = m, curve_extrap = ex))
    adg_of <- function(dd) {
      if (data.table::uniqueN(dd$date) < 10L) return(NA_real_)
      tryCatch(suppressWarnings(adg_one_pig(dd, q, day0)$adg), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    }
    full <- adg_of(d)
    last_day <- max(d$date)
    for (td in trim_days) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
        type = c(paste0("late", td), paste0("early", td)), model = lab,
        rmse = NA_real_, mae = NA_real_,
        adg = c(adg_of(d[date >= first_day + td]), adg_of(d[date <= last_day - td])),
        adg_full = full)
    }
  }
  data.table::rbindlist(rows)
}

#' Validate Body Weight Fill Methods
#'
#' @description
#' Hide recorded daily weights of the stage on purpose, fill them again with
#' each method and compare with the recorded values. Errors are measured on
#' the hidden days (filled minus recorded daily weight) and on ADG (against
#' the ADG of all records with the settings of `weight`).
#'
#' @param weight Result of [clean_weight()].
#' @param methods Fill methods to compare:
#'   - `"linear"`: linear interpolation between recorded days, the growth
#'     curve `curve_model` of the settings before the first and after the
#'     last recorded day (the method of [calc_adg()]);
#'   - `"poly1"`, `"poly2"`, `"poly3"`, `"gompertz"`: that growth curve,
#'     fitted on the remaining records, for every missing day.
#' @param extrap Extrapolations of the curve beyond the records to compare
#'   (values of `curve_extrap`): `"start"`, `"curve"`, `"tangent"` or
#'   several. Default: the one of the settings of `weight`. Other than
#'   `"curve"`, a method is labelled e.g. `"linear+tangent"`. It
#'   matters for the days hidden at the ends (`"late<d>"`, `"early<d>"`).
#' @param scenarios Patterns of hidden days, as in [validate_adfi()]:
#'   `"random<p>"`, `"blocks<n>"`, `"late<d>"`, `"early<d>"`. Only recorded
#'   stage days are hidden.
#' @param reps Number of repetitions per scenario. Default 3.
#' @param max_pigs Use a random sample of at most this many pigs. Default
#'   `NULL`: all.
#' @param seed Random seed.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary and progress, default).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores. Default 1.
#'
#' @return A list of class `ppt_validation` with
#' - `summary`: one row per scenario and method: `daily_rmse` and
#'   `daily_mae` (kg, hidden days), `daily_bias` (kg), `adg_bias` and
#'   `adg_rmse` (g/d), `adg_spearman` (rank correlation with the full-data
#'   ADG) and `n_pigs`;
#' - `per_pig`: the errors of every pig, scenario, repetition and method;
#' - `settings`.
#' @export
validate_weight_fill <- function(weight, methods = c("linear", "poly1", "poly2", "poly3", "gompertz"),
                                 extrap = NULL,
                                 scenarios = c("random30", "blocks3", "late20", "early15"),
                                 reps = 3, max_pigs = NULL, seed = 1, verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  local_cores(cores)
  if (!inherits(weight, "ppt_weight")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg weight} must be the result of {.fn clean_weight}.")
  }
  qc <- weight$settings
  ok_methods <- c("linear", "poly1", "poly2", "poly3", "gompertz")
  if (!is.character(methods) || length(methods) == 0L || !all(methods %in% ok_methods)) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg methods} must be one or more of {.val {ok_methods}}.")
  }
  extrap <- extrap %||% qc$curve_extrap %||% "curve"
  for (e in extrap) qc_validate(qc_set(qc, list(curve_extrap = e)))
  configs <- curve_configs(methods, extrap)
  sc <- parse_scenarios(scenarios)
  ppt_msg("Validating weight fill methods ({length(scenarios)} scenario{?s} x {reps} repetition{?s})", "h1")

  set.seed(seed)
  kept <- sample_pigs(weight$per_pig[status != "removed", responder], max_pigs)
  rec <- weight$records[outlier == FALSE & responder %in% kept,
                        .(responder, date, entry_time, weight)]
  data.table::setorder(rec, responder, entry_time)
  day0 <- weight$daily[, min(date - seq_days + 1L)]
  # hidden days, drawn once per pig so that results do not depend on `cores`
  pigs <- split(rec, by = "responder")
  masks <- lapply(pigs, function(d) {
    full <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(adg_one_pig(d, qc, day0)), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(full) || is.na(full$adg)) return(NULL)
    st <- full$daily[[1L]][in_stage == TRUE]
    list(adg_full = full$adg, days = st$date, observed = st$source == "observed",
         truth = st$weight, masks = make_masks(st$source == "observed", sc, reps))
  })
  rec[, info := list(masks[responder])]
  rec <- rec[!vapply(info, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (nrow(rec) == 0L) cli::cli_abort("No pig with an ADG to validate.")
  fits <- fit_by_pig(rec, validate_fill_one_pig, step = "validate_weight_fill", qc = qc,
                     configs = configs, day0 = day0)
  per_pig <- fits$result
  summary <- per_pig[, .(
    daily_rmse = sqrt(sum(sq_err, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(n_hidden)),
    daily_mae = sum(abs_err, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(n_hidden),
    daily_bias = sum(sum_err, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(n_hidden),
    adg_bias = mean(adg - adg_full, na.rm = TRUE),
    adg_rmse = sqrt(mean((adg - adg_full)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    n_pigs = data.table::uniqueN(responder[!is.na(adg)])
  ), by = .(scenario, method)]
  rho <- per_pig[!is.na(adg), .(
    adg_spearman = if (.N > 2L) stats::cor(adg, adg_full, method = "spearman") else NA_real_
  ), by = .(scenario, method, rep)][, .(adg_spearman = mean(adg_spearman, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(scenario, method)]
  summary <- rho[summary, on = c("scenario", "method")]
  data.table::setcolorder(summary, c("scenario", "method", "daily_rmse", "daily_mae", "daily_bias",
                                     "adg_bias", "adg_rmse", "adg_spearman", "n_pigs"))
  summary <- summary[order(match(scenario, scenarios), match(method, configs$label))]
  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L) {
    ppt_msg("{data.table::uniqueN(per_pig$responder)} pig{?s} used", "info")
  }
  structure(list(summary = summary, per_pig = per_pig, failed = fits$failed,
                 settings = list(qc = qc, methods = methods, extrap = extrap,
                                 scenarios = scenarios, reps = reps, seed = seed)),
            class = c("ppt_validation", "ppt_result"))
}

# Fill of one pig under every mask and method for validate_weight_fill().
validate_fill_one_pig <- function(d, qc, configs, day0) {
  info <- d$info[[1L]]
  d <- d[, .(date, entry_time, weight)]
  rows <- list()
  for (mk in info$masks) {
    hidden_days <- info$days[mk$hide]
    dd <- d[!date %in% hidden_days]
    truth <- info$truth[mk$hide]
    for (ci in seq_len(nrow(configs))) {
      m <- configs$model[ci]
      q <- qc_set(qc, if (m == "linear") list(curve_extrap = configs$extrap[ci])
                      else list(curve_model = m, curve_extrap = configs$extrap[ci]))
      res <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(adg_one_pig(dd, q, day0, fill = if (m == "linear") "linear" else "curve")),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
      err <- rep(NA_real_, length(truth))
      adg <- NA_real_
      if (!is.null(res)) {
        dl <- res$daily[[1L]]
        est <- dl$weight_filled[match(hidden_days, dl$date)]
        miss <- is.na(est)
        if (any(miss)) {
          # hidden days outside the new stage: from the curve
          est[miss] <- dl$predicted[match(hidden_days[miss], dl$date)]
        }
        err <- est - truth
        adg <- res$adg
      }
      ok <- !is.na(err)
      rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
        scenario = mk$scenario, rep = mk$rep, method = configs$label[ci],
        adg = adg, adg_full = info$adg_full,
        sq_err = sum(err[ok]^2), abs_err = sum(abs(err[ok])), sum_err = sum(err[ok]),
        n_hidden = sum(ok))
    }
  }
  data.table::rbindlist(rows)
}

#' Validate Feed Intake Imputation
#'
#' @description
#' Hide recorded daily feed intake on purpose, impute it again and compare
#' with the recorded values. Only pigs whose stage is well covered by records
#' are used, and errors are measured on the recorded days only.
#'
#' @param adfi Result of [calc_adfi()].
#' @param methods Imputation methods to compare (values of `impute_method`).
#'   For `"loess_pop"`, the population curve of each pig is fitted without
#'   that pig (leave-one-out), so its hidden days do not inform the curve.
#' @param scenarios Patterns of hidden days:
#'   - `"random<p>"`: `p`% of the recorded days at random, e.g. `"random30"`;
#'   - `"blocks<n>"`: `n` blocks of 3-10 consecutive days, e.g. `"blocks3"`;
#'   - `"late<d>"`: the first `d` days of the stage (late entry);
#'   - `"early<d>"`: the last `d` days of the stage (early exit).
#' @param reps Number of repetitions per scenario. Default 5.
#' @param min_coverage Pigs with at least this share of recorded stage days
#'   are used. Default 0.8.
#' @param max_pigs Use a random sample of at most this many of these pigs.
#'   Default `NULL`: all.
#' @param seed Random seed.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary and progress, default).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores. Default 1.
#'
#' @return A list of class `ppt_validation` with
#' - `summary`: one row per scenario and method: `mean_abs_error_pct` and
#'   `p95_abs_error_pct` (error of the ADFI of each pig, % of the recorded
#'   ADFI), `bias_pct`, `spearman` (rank correlation of ADFI with the
#'   recorded ADFI), `daily_rmse` (g/d, hidden days) and `n_pigs`;
#' - `per_pig`: the error of every pig, scenario, repetition and method;
#' - `settings`.
#' @export
validate_adfi <- function(adfi, methods = c("loess_pop", "loess_lm", "linear"),
                          scenarios = c("random30", "blocks3", "late20", "early15"),
                          reps = 5, min_coverage = 0.8, max_pigs = NULL, seed = 1,
                          verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  local_cores(cores)
  if (!inherits(adfi, "ppt_adfi")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg adfi} must be the result of {.fn calc_adfi}.")
  }
  qc <- adfi$settings
  for (m in methods) qc_validate(qc_set(qc, list(impute_method = m)))
  sc <- parse_scenarios(scenarios)
  ppt_msg("Validating feed intake imputation ({length(scenarios)} scenario{?s} x {reps} repetition{?s})", "h1")

  pigs <- adfi$per_pig[coverage >= min_coverage, responder]
  if (length(pigs) < 3L) {
    cli::cli_abort("Only {length(pigs)} pig{?s} with coverage >= {min_coverage}; lower {.arg min_coverage}.")
  }
  set.seed(seed)
  pigs <- sample_pigs(pigs, max_pigs)
  d <- adfi$daily[responder %in% pigs & in_stage == TRUE,
                  .(responder, date, seq_days, bw, in_stage, dfi, state)]
  d[, observed := state %in% c("org", "corr")]
  d[, dfi_true := data.table::fifelse(observed, dfi, NA_real_)]
  data.table::setorder(d, responder, date)
  # leave-one-out population curves, keyed by pig
  pop <- NULL
  if ("loess_pop" %in% methods) {
    breeds <- if ("breed" %in% names(adfi$per_pig)) adfi$per_pig[, .(responder, breed)] else NULL
    pop <- pop_curves_loo(d[observed == TRUE & !is.na(bw), .(responder, dfi = dfi_true, bw)],
                          pigs, breeds)
    d[, pop_key := responder]
  }

  # hidden days, drawn once so that results do not depend on `cores`
  d[, masks := list(list(make_masks(observed, sc, reps))), by = responder]
  fits <- fit_by_pig(d, validate_adfi_one_pig, step = "validate_adfi", qc = qc,
                     methods = methods, pop = pop)
  per_pig <- fits$result
  summary <- per_pig[!is.na(err_pct), .(
    mean_abs_error_pct = mean(abs(err_pct)),
    p95_abs_error_pct = stats::quantile(abs(err_pct), 0.95, names = FALSE),
    bias_pct = mean(err_pct),
    daily_rmse = sqrt(sum(sq_err, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(n_hidden)),
    n_pigs = data.table::uniqueN(responder)
  ), by = .(scenario, method)]
  rho <- per_pig[!is.na(adfi_est), .(
    spearman = if (.N > 2L) stats::cor(adfi_est, adfi_true, method = "spearman") else NA_real_
  ), by = .(scenario, method, rep)][, .(spearman = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(scenario, method)]
  summary <- summary[rho, on = c("scenario", "method")]
  data.table::setcolorder(summary, c("scenario", "method", "mean_abs_error_pct",
                                     "p95_abs_error_pct", "bias_pct", "spearman"))
  summary <- summary[order(match(scenario, scenarios), match(method, methods))]

  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L) {
    ppt_msg("{length(pigs)} pig{?s} with coverage >= {min_coverage} used", "info")
  }
  structure(list(summary = summary, per_pig = per_pig, failed = fits$failed,
                 settings = list(qc = qc, methods = methods, scenarios = scenarios,
                                 reps = reps, min_coverage = min_coverage, seed = seed)),
            class = c("ppt_validation", "ppt_result"))
}

# Population curve of each pig fitted on the other pigs (of its breed when
# the breed has at least `min_pigs` other pigs), named by pig.
pop_curves_loo <- function(rec, pigs, breeds = NULL, min_pigs = 10L) {
  if (!is.null(breeds)) rec <- merge(rec, breeds, by = "responder", all.x = TRUE)
  out <- lapply(pigs, function(p) {
    o <- rec[responder != p]
    if (!is.null(breeds)) {
      b <- breeds[responder == p, breed][1L]
      ob <- o[breed %in% b]
      if (!is.na(b) && data.table::uniqueN(ob$responder) >= min_pigs) o <- ob
    }
    fit_pop_curve(o$dfi, o$bw, data.table::uniqueN(o$responder))
  })
  names(out) <- pigs
  out[!vapply(out, is.null, logical(1))]
}

# A random sample of at most `max_pigs` pig IDs (all when NULL).
sample_pigs <- function(ids, max_pigs) {
  if (is.null(max_pigs) || length(ids) <= max_pigs) return(ids)
  sort(sample(ids, max_pigs))
}

# "random30" -> list(type = "random", value = 30)
parse_scenarios <- function(scenarios) {
  ok <- grepl("^(random|blocks|late|early)[0-9]+$", scenarios)
  if (!is.character(scenarios) || length(scenarios) == 0L || !all(ok)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c("Unknown scenario{?s}: {.val {scenarios[!ok]}}.",
                     "i" = "Use random<p>, blocks<n>, late<d> or early<d>, e.g. {.val random30}."))
  }
  stats::setNames(lapply(scenarios, function(s) list(
    type = sub("[0-9]+$", "", s), value = as.numeric(sub("^[a-z]+", "", s)))), scenarios)
}

# Logical masks (hidden recorded days) for every scenario and repetition.
make_masks <- function(observed, sc, reps) {
  n <- length(observed)
  obs <- which(observed)
  out <- list()
  for (nm in names(sc)) {
    s <- sc[[nm]]
    for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
      hide <- rep(FALSE, n)
      if (s$type == "random") {
        hide[obs[stats::runif(length(obs)) < s$value / 100]] <- TRUE
      } else if (s$type == "blocks") {
        for (b in seq_len(s$value)) {
          len <- sample(3:10, 1L)
          start <- sample.int(max(1L, n - len), 1L)
          hide[start:min(n, start + len - 1L)] <- TRUE
        }
        hide <- hide & observed
      } else if (s$type == "late") {
        hide[seq_len(min(n, s$value))] <- TRUE
        hide <- hide & observed
      } else {
        hide[seq_len(n) > n - s$value] <- TRUE
        hide <- hide & observed
      }
      out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- list(scenario = nm, rep = r, hide = hide)
    }
  }
  out
}

# Imputation of one pig under every mask and method for validate_adfi().
validate_adfi_one_pig <- function(d, qc, methods, pop = NULL) {
  masks <- d$masks[[1L]]
  truth <- mean(d$dfi_true, na.rm = TRUE)
  rows <- vector("list", length(masks) * length(methods))
  i <- 0L
  for (mk in masks) {
    dd <- d[, intersect(c("date", "seq_days", "bw", "in_stage", "dfi_true", "observed", "pop_key"), names(d)), with = FALSE]
    dd[, dfi_check := data.table::fifelse(mk$hide, NA_real_, dfi_true)]
    dd[, state := data.table::fifelse(is.na(dfi_check), NA_character_, "org")]
    for (m in methods) {
      i <- i + 1L
      q <- qc_set(qc, list(impute_method = m))
      im <- tryCatch(impute_dfi_one_pig(dd, q, pop = pop), error = function(e) NULL)
      est <- if (is.null(im)) NA_real_ else im$dfi
      hidden <- mk$hide & !is.na(est)
      adfi_est <- if (is.null(im) || any(is.na(est[dd$observed]))) NA_real_ else mean(est[dd$observed])
      rows[[i]] <- data.table::data.table(
        scenario = mk$scenario, rep = mk$rep, method = m,
        adfi_true = truth, adfi_est = adfi_est,
        err_pct = 100 * (adfi_est - truth) / truth,
        sq_err = sum((est[hidden] - dd$dfi_true[hidden])^2),
        n_hidden = sum(hidden)
      )
    }
  }
  data.table::rbindlist(rows)
}

#' @export
print.ppt_validation <- function(x, ...) {
  cli::cli_h2("{.cls ppt_validation}")
  s <- data.table::copy(x$summary)
  num <- names(s)[vapply(s, is.double, logical(1))]
  if (length(num) > 0L) s[, (num) := lapply(.SD, signif, 3), .SDcols = num]
  print(s)
  invisible(x)
}
```

```{r example-validate}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
w <- clean_weight(visits, verbose = 0)

# 1. weight outlier methods: 5% artificial errors of 3-15 kg
vo <- validate_outliers(visits, reps = 1)
vo$summary

# 2. growth curve models
va <- validate_adg(w, models = c("poly1", "poly2", "poly3"))
va$summary

# 3. weight fill methods
vw <- validate_weight_fill(w, methods = c("linear", "poly2"), scenarios = c("blocks3", "late20"), reps = 1)
vw$summary

# 4. feed intake imputation
adfi <- calc_adfi(visits, calc_adg(w, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
vf <- validate_adfi(adfi, scenarios = c("random30", "late20"), reps = 2)
vf$summary
```

```{r tests-validate}
test_that("validate_outliers finds artificial errors", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_outliers(v, methods = list(rlm = "rlm", sd = "sd", track = "track"), rate = 0.05,
                           size = c(10, 20), reps = 1, verbose = 0)
  expect_s3_class(res, "ppt_validation")
  expect_equal(res$summary$method, c("none", "rlm", "sd", "track"))
  expect_true(outlier_qc(qc_config(), "track")$weight_track)
  expect_false(outlier_qc(qc_config(), "rlm")$weight_track)
  expect_equal(outlier_qc(qc_config(), c("track", "sd"))$weight_outlier, "sd")
  s <- res$summary
  expect_lt(s[method == "none", sensitivity], 0.1)   # weight_range only
  expect_gt(s[method == "rlm", sensitivity], 0.8)
  expect_lt(s[method == "rlm", false_positive_rate], 0.1)
  expect_true(all(abs(s$adg_bias) < 20))
  # reproducible
  again <- validate_outliers(v, methods = list(rlm = "rlm", sd = "sd", track = "track"), rate = 0.05,
                             size = c(10, 20), reps = 1, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(again$summary, res$summary, check.attributes = FALSE)
  down <- validate_outliers(v, methods = list(rlm = "rlm"), direction = "down",
                            reps = 1, verbose = 0)
  expect_gt(down$summary[method == "rlm", sensitivity], 0.5)
  expect_error(validate_outliers(v, methods = list("rlm")), "named list")
  expect_error(validate_outliers(v, methods = list(x = "nope")), "weight_outlier")
})

test_that("validate_adg compares curve models", {
  w <- clean_weight(prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_adg(w, models = c("poly1", "poly2"), extrap = "curve", trim_days = 10, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(res$summary$model, c("poly1", "poly2"))
  expect_true(all(c("cv_rmse", "cv_mae", "bias_late10", "rmse_early10",
                    "spearman_late10", "n_early10") %in% names(res$summary)))
  expect_true(all(res$summary$cv_rmse > 0 & res$summary$cv_rmse < 5))
  expect_equal(nrow(res$cv), 2L * w$per_pig[status != "removed", .N])
  # same folds whatever the number of cores
  skip_on_os("windows")
  two <- validate_adg(w, models = c("poly1", "poly2"), extrap = "curve", trim_days = 10, verbose = 0, cores = 2)
  expect_equal(two$summary, res$summary, check.attributes = FALSE)
  expect_error(validate_adg(w, models = "nope"), "curve_model")
})

test_that("validate_weight_fill compares weight fill methods", {
  w <- clean_weight(prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_weight_fill(w, methods = c("linear", "poly2"), extrap = "curve",
                              scenarios = c("random30", "blocks3", "late20"), reps = 1, verbose = 0)
  s <- res$summary
  expect_equal(nrow(s), 6L)
  expect_true(all(c("daily_rmse", "daily_mae", "adg_bias", "adg_rmse", "adg_spearman") %in% names(s)))
  expect_true(all(s$daily_rmse > 0 & s$daily_rmse < 10))
  # linear interpolation is close to the recorded weight for random gaps
  expect_lt(s[scenario == "random30" & method == "linear", daily_rmse], 2)
  expect_true(all(is.finite(s$adg_rmse)))
  expect_error(validate_weight_fill(w, methods = "loess"), "methods")
  expect_error(validate_weight_fill(list()), "clean_weight")
})

test_that("validate_adfi measures imputation error", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  a <- calc_adg(clean_weight(v, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  f <- calc_adfi(v, a, verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_adfi(f, scenarios = c("random30", "late20", "blocks3", "early10"),
                       reps = 2, verbose = 0)
  s <- res$summary
  expect_equal(nrow(s), 12L)
  expect_true(all(s$n_pigs >= 3L))
  expect_true(all(s$mean_abs_error_pct < 15))
  # random gaps cost less than a long gap at the start
  expect_lt(s[scenario == "random30" & method == "loess_lm", p95_abs_error_pct],
            s[scenario == "late20" & method == "loess_lm", p95_abs_error_pct])
  expect_setequal(unique(s$method), c("loess_pop", "loess_lm", "linear"))
  expect_error(validate_adfi(f, scenarios = "rand"), "scenario")
  expect_error(validate_adfi(f, min_coverage = 1.01), "coverage")
})

test_that("max_pigs uses a sample of pigs", {
  w <- clean_weight(prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_adg(w, models = "poly2", trim_days = 10, max_pigs = 5, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(nrow(res$cv), 5L)
  expect_equal(sample_pigs(letters[1:3], NULL), letters[1:3])
})

test_that("make_masks hides only recorded days", {
  set.seed(1)
  obs <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, rep(TRUE, 27))
  m <- make_masks(obs, parse_scenarios(c("late5", "early5", "blocks2", "random50")), reps = 1)
  expect_length(m, 4L)
  for (x in m) expect_false(any(x$hide & !obs))
  expect_equal(which(m[[1]]$hide), c(1L, 2L, 4L, 5L))
  expect_equal(which(m[[2]]$hide), 26:30)
})

test_that("validate_adg and validate_weight_fill compare extrapolations", {
  w <- clean_weight(prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0), verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_adg(w, models = "poly2", extrap = c("curve", "tangent"), trim_days = 20,
                      max_pigs = 8, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(res$summary$model, c("poly2", "poly2+tangent"))
  expect_equal(validate_adg(w, models = "poly2", trim_days = 10, max_pigs = 4, verbose = 0)$summary$model,
               "poly2+start")
  # cross-validation mostly predicts inside the records: nearly the same
  expect_equal(res$summary$cv_rmse[1], res$summary$cv_rmse[2], tolerance = 0.05)
  fill <- validate_weight_fill(w, methods = "linear", extrap = c("curve", "tangent"),
                               scenarios = "late20", reps = 1, max_pigs = 8, verbose = 0)
  expect_setequal(fill$summary$method, c("linear", "linear+tangent"))
  expect_error(validate_adg(w, extrap = "line", verbose = 0), "curve_extrap")
})
```

# validate_truncation

`validate_truncation()` checks the whole pipeline **without information
leaking back** from hidden data. It removes every visit (body weight and
feed) of part of the pigs over some days of the stage, as if they had
entered late, left early or missed a stretch of the test, reruns
`clean_weight()`, `calc_adg()`, `calc_adfi()` and `calc_fcr()`, and compares
ADG, ADFI and FCR of these pigs with the result of all data. Each pig is
truncated once per repetition while the other pigs keep their records, so
population curves and the correction model still see the whole stage, as in
a real batch where only some pigs have missing ends. Several QC settings
can be compared on the same hidden data.

The other validation functions are faster but look at one step at a time,
with the rest of the data known: `validate_adfi()` keeps the body weight of
the hidden feed days and the stage of the full data, `validate_adg()` and
`validate_weight_fill()` use weight records cleaned with all data. They are
somewhat optimistic, most of all at the stage ends.

```{r function-validate_truncation}
#' Validate the Whole Pipeline by Truncating Pigs
#'
#' @description
#' Remove all visits of part of the pigs over some days of the stage (late
#' entry, early exit or a gap), rerun the pipeline from [clean_weight()] to
#' [calc_fcr()] with each QC setting, and compare ADG, ADFI and FCR with the
#' result of all data. Nothing of the hidden days is used, so the result
#' measures what really happens when a pig misses these days.
#'
#' @param visits Result of [prep_visits()].
#' @param settings A QC object from [qc_config()], or a named list of them
#'   to compare, e.g. `list(lm = qc_config(impute_method = "loess_lm"),
#'   pop = qc_config())`.
#' @param scenarios Days removed, counted on the stage of the first setting
#'   (from its full-data run):
#'   - `"late<d>"`: the first `d` days of the stage and everything before
#'     (late entry), e.g. `"late20"`;
#'   - `"early<d>"`: the last `d` days of the stage and everything after
#'     (early exit);
#'   - `"gap<d>"`: `d` consecutive days in the middle of the stage.
#' @param share Share of the pigs truncated in one run (default 0.5). The
#'   pigs are split at random into `round(1 / share)` groups, each group is
#'   truncated in turn, so every pig is truncated once per repetition.
#' @param reps Number of repetitions, each with a new random split.
#'   Default 5.
#' @param top Share of the best pigs for the selection agreement `top_agree`
#'   (default 0.2: the best 20%). Best = highest ADG, lowest FCR, highest
#'   ADFI.
#' @param pigs Pigs to truncate. Default `NULL`: pigs whose stage is fully
#'   covered by records in the first setting (`adg_type == "observed"`) and
#'   that have an FCR.
#' @param seed Random seed.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent) or 1 (progress, default).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores: runs of the pipeline in parallel.
#'
#' @return A list of class `ppt_validation` with
#' - `summary`: one row per setting, scenario and trait (`adg`, `adfi`,
#'   `fcr`): the mean over repetitions of `bias` (truncated - full),
#'   `rmse`, `mae_pct` (mean absolute error, % of the full value),
#'   `pearson` and `spearman` correlation with the full value, `slope` of
#'   the regression of the truncated on the full value (below 1: the
#'   differences between pigs shrink), `top_agree` (share of the best `top`
#'   pigs on full data that are also among the best after truncation),
#'   `n` (pigs with both values) and `n_lost` (pigs that lost their value);
#'   columns ending in `_sd` give the SD over repetitions;
#' - `per_rep`: the same measures for every repetition;
#' - `per_pig`: full and truncated value of every pig, trait, setting,
#'   scenario and repetition;
#' - `settings`.
#'
#' @details
#' The reference is the result of all data with the same setting, not the
#' unknown true value: the measures tell how stable a setting is when data
#' are missing, which is what matters to compare settings. With few pigs
#' (e.g. 20), differences of a few hundredths in a correlation are noise;
#' look at the `_sd` columns and use more repetitions.
#'
#' Pigs whose test becomes too short after truncation (e.g. below
#' `min_test_days`) are removed by [clean_weight()] and counted in
#' `n_lost`.
#'
#' @seealso [validate_adfi()], [validate_adg()] for faster checks of single
#'   steps.
#' @export
validate_truncation <- function(visits, settings = qc_config(),
                                scenarios = c("late10", "late20", "early10", "early20", "gap10"),
                                share = 0.5, reps = 5, top = 0.2, pigs = NULL,
                                seed = 1, verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  dt <- as_dt(visits, "visits")
  check_cols(dt, c("responder", "identified", "location", "date", "entry_time", "weight"),
             arg = "visits", hint = "Use {.fn prep_visits} first.")
  if (inherits(settings, "ppt_qc")) settings <- list(settings = settings)
  if (!is.list(settings) || length(settings) == 0L || is.null(names(settings)) ||
      any(!nzchar(names(settings))) || anyDuplicated(names(settings)) ||
      !all(vapply(settings, inherits, logical(1), "ppt_qc"))) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg settings} must be a {.fn qc_config} object or a named list of them.")
  }
  sc <- parse_truncation(scenarios)
  if (!is.numeric(share) || length(share) != 1L || share <= 0 || share > 0.5) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg share} must be a number in (0, 0.5].")
  }
  if (!is.numeric(reps) || length(reps) != 1L || reps < 1) cli::cli_abort("{.arg reps} must be at least 1.")
  if (!is.numeric(top) || length(top) != 1L || top <= 0 || top >= 1) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg top} must be a number between 0 and 1.")
  }
  cores <- check_cores(cores)

  ppt_msg("Validating the pipeline by truncation ({length(settings)} setting{?s} x {length(scenarios)} scenario{?s} x {reps} repetition{?s})", "h1")
  full <- lapply(settings, function(q) pipeline_run(dt, q))
  stage <- full[[1L]]$stage
  ok <- stage[adg_type == "observed" & !is.na(start_date) & !is.na(end_date), responder]
  ok <- intersect(ok, full[[1L]]$traits[!is.na(fcr), responder])
  pigs <- if (is.null(pigs)) ok else intersect(as.character(pigs), ok)
  if (length(pigs) < 6L) {
    cli::cli_abort("Only {length(pigs)} pig{?s} with a fully covered stage; at least 6 are needed.")
  }
  stage <- stage[responder %in% pigs, .(responder, start_date, end_date)]

  # one job = one setting x scenario x repetition x group of truncated pigs
  set.seed(seed)
  n_groups <- max(2L, round(1 / share))
  splits <- lapply(seq_len(reps), function(r) {
    split(sample(pigs), rep_len(seq_len(n_groups), length(pigs)))
  })
  jobs <- list()
  for (s in names(settings)) for (nm in names(sc)) for (r in seq_len(reps)) for (g in splits[[r]]) {
    jobs[[length(jobs) + 1L]] <- list(setting = s, scenario = nm, rep = r, pigs = g)
  }
  res <- run_with_progress(jobs, truncation_job, cores = cores, label = "Truncated runs",
                           visits = dt, settings = settings, sc = sc, stage = stage)
  bad <- vapply(res, inherits, logical(1), "error")
  if (any(bad)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c("{sum(bad)} truncated run{?s} failed.", "x" = conditionMessage(res[[which(bad)[1L]]])))
  }
  trunc <- data.table::rbindlist(res)
  ref <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(names(full), function(s) {
    data.table::melt(full[[s]]$traits[responder %in% pigs], id.vars = "responder",
                     variable.name = "trait", value.name = "full", variable.factor = FALSE)[, setting := s]
  }))
  per_pig <- merge(ref, trunc, by = c("setting", "responder", "trait"), all.y = TRUE)
  data.table::setcolorder(per_pig, c("setting", "scenario", "rep", "trait", "responder", "full", "truncated"))

  per_rep <- per_pig[, truncation_measures(full, truncated, trait[1L], top),
                     by = .(setting, scenario, rep, trait)]
  meas <- c("bias", "rmse", "mae_pct", "pearson", "spearman", "slope", "top_agree")
  summary <- per_rep[, c(lapply(.SD[, meas, with = FALSE], mean, na.rm = TRUE),
                         stats::setNames(lapply(.SD[, meas, with = FALSE], stats::sd, na.rm = TRUE),
                                         paste0(meas, "_sd")),
                         list(n = mean(n), n_lost = mean(n_lost))),
                     by = .(setting, scenario, trait)]
  for (col in names(summary)) {
    if (is.double(summary[[col]])) data.table::set(summary, j = col, value = data.table::fifelse(is.nan(summary[[col]]), NA_real_, summary[[col]]))
  }
  summary <- summary[order(match(trait, c("adg", "adfi", "fcr")), match(scenario, scenarios),
                           match(setting, names(settings)))]
  data.table::setcolorder(summary, c("setting", "scenario", "trait", meas, "n", "n_lost"))

  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L) {
    ppt_msg("{length(pigs)} pig{?s} truncated in {length(jobs)} run{?s} of the pipeline", "info")
  }
  structure(list(summary = summary, per_rep = per_rep, per_pig = per_pig,
                 settings = list(qc = settings, scenarios = scenarios, share = share, reps = reps,
                                 top = top, pigs = pigs, seed = seed)),
            class = c("ppt_validation", "ppt_result"))
}

# "late20" -> list(type = "late", days = 20)
parse_truncation <- function(scenarios) {
  ok <- is.character(scenarios) & grepl("^(late|early|gap)[0-9]+$", scenarios)
  if (!is.character(scenarios) || length(scenarios) == 0L || !all(ok) || anyDuplicated(scenarios)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c("Unknown or repeated scenario{?s}: {.val {scenarios[!ok | duplicated(scenarios)]}}.",
                     "i" = "Use late<d>, early<d> or gap<d>, e.g. {.val late20}."))
  }
  stats::setNames(lapply(scenarios, function(s) {
    list(type = sub("[0-9]+$", "", s), days = as.numeric(sub("^[a-z]+", "", s)))
  }), scenarios)
}

# The pipeline from clean_weight() to calc_fcr(): ADG, ADFI, FCR per pig and
# the stage of each pig.
pipeline_run <- function(visits, qc) {
  w <- clean_weight(visits, qc, verbose = 0)
  a <- calc_adg(w, qc, verbose = 0)
  f <- calc_adfi(visits, a, qc, verbose = 0)
  r <- calc_fcr(a, f, verbose = 0)
  list(traits = r$per_pig[, .(responder, adg, adfi, fcr)],
       stage = a$per_pig[, .(responder, adg_type, start_date, end_date)])
}

# One truncated run of the pipeline for validate_truncation().
truncation_job <- function(job, visits, settings, sc, stage) {
  hide <- truncation_hide(visits, stage[responder %in% job$pigs], sc[[job$scenario]])
  out <- pipeline_run(visits[!hide], settings[[job$setting]])$traits
  out <- merge(data.table::data.table(responder = job$pigs), out, by = "responder", all.x = TRUE)
  out <- data.table::melt(out, id.vars = "responder", variable.name = "trait",
                          value.name = "truncated", variable.factor = FALSE)
  out[, `:=`(setting = job$setting, scenario = job$scenario, rep = job$rep)]
  out[]
}

# Identified visits of the pigs in `stage` on the days of scenario `s`.
truncation_hide <- function(visits, stage, s) {
  i <- match(visits$responder, stage$responder)
  start <- stage$start_date[i]
  end <- stage$end_date[i]
  d <- visits$date
  inside <- visits$identified %in% TRUE & !is.na(start)
  inside & switch(s$type,
    late = d < start + s$days,
    early = d > end - s$days,
    gap = {
      mid <- start + floor(as.numeric(end - start) / 2) - floor(s$days / 2)
      d >= mid & d < mid + s$days
    })
}

# Agreement of truncated with full values of one trait.
truncation_measures <- function(full, truncated, trait, top) {
  ok <- !is.na(full) & !is.na(truncated)
  n <- sum(ok)
  lost <- sum(!is.na(full) & is.na(truncated))
  if (n < 3L) {
    return(list(bias = NA_real_, rmse = NA_real_, mae_pct = NA_real_, pearson = NA_real_,
                spearman = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_, top_agree = NA_real_, n = n, n_lost = lost))
  }
  x <- full[ok]
  y <- truncated[ok]
  sgn <- if (trait == "fcr") -1 else 1        # best = lowest FCR
  k <- max(1L, round(top * n))
  best_full <- order(-sgn * x)[seq_len(k)]
  best_trunc <- order(-sgn * y)[seq_len(k)]
  list(
    bias = mean(y - x),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((y - x)^2)),
    mae_pct = 100 * mean(abs(y - x) / abs(x)),
    pearson = if (stats::sd(x) > 0 && stats::sd(y) > 0) stats::cor(x, y) else NA_real_,
    spearman = if (stats::sd(x) > 0 && stats::sd(y) > 0) stats::cor(x, y, method = "spearman") else NA_real_,
    slope = if (stats::var(x) > 0) stats::cov(x, y) / stats::var(x) else NA_real_,
    top_agree = length(intersect(best_full, best_trunc)) / k,
    n = n, n_lost = lost
  )
}
```

```{r example-validate_truncation}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
# 2 settings x 1 scenario x 1 repetition; use more repetitions on real data
res <- validate_truncation(
  visits,
  settings = list(lm = qc_config(impute_method = "loess_lm"), pop = qc_config()),
  scenarios = "late20", reps = 1
)
res$summary[, .(setting, trait, mae_pct, spearman, slope, top_agree)]
```

```{r tests-validate_truncation}
test_that("validate_truncation compares settings without leakage", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  res <- validate_truncation(v, settings = list(lm = qc_config(impute_method = "loess_lm"), pop = qc_config()),
                             scenarios = c("late20", "gap10"), reps = 2, verbose = 0)
  s <- res$summary
  expect_equal(nrow(s), 2L * 2L * 3L)
  expect_setequal(s$trait, c("adg", "adfi", "fcr"))
  expect_true(all(c("bias", "rmse", "mae_pct", "pearson", "spearman", "slope", "top_agree",
                    "n", "n_lost", "rmse_sd", "slope_sd") %in% names(s)))
  expect_true(all(s$spearman > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE))
  # every pig is truncated once per repetition and setting
  pp <- res$per_pig[trait == "adg"]
  expect_equal(pp[, .N, by = .(setting, scenario, rep)]$N, rep(length(res$settings$pigs), 8L))
  expect_false(anyDuplicated(pp[, .(setting, scenario, rep, responder)]) > 0)
  # the same settings give the same ADG (they differ only in the feed imputation)
  expect_equal(s[setting == "lm" & trait == "adg", rmse], s[setting == "pop" & trait == "adg", rmse])
  # a gap in the middle costs less ADG than a late entry
  expect_lt(s[setting == "lm" & trait == "adg" & scenario == "gap10", rmse],
            s[setting == "lm" & trait == "adg" & scenario == "late20", rmse])
})

test_that("truncation removes the right days", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  st <- data.table::data.table(responder = "13913", start_date = as.Date("2024-03-01"),
                               end_date = as.Date("2024-05-01"))
  sc <- parse_truncation(c("late10", "early10", "gap10"))
  kept <- function(s) unique(v[!truncation_hide(v, st, sc[[s]]) & responder %in% "13913", date])
  expect_false(any(kept("late10") < as.Date("2024-03-11")))
  expect_false(any(kept("early10") > as.Date("2024-04-21")))
  g <- kept("gap10")
  # 61-day stage: middle on day 30 (31 March), 10 days from 26 March to 4 April
  expect_false(any(g >= as.Date("2024-03-26") & g < as.Date("2024-04-05")))
  expect_true(as.Date("2024-03-25") %in% g && as.Date("2024-04-05") %in% g)
  # other pigs and unidentified visits are never removed
  h <- truncation_hide(v, st, sc[["late10"]])
  expect_true(all(v$responder[h] == "13913"))
  expect_false(any(h & !v$identified))
})

test_that("truncation_measures and bad inputs", {
  m <- truncation_measures(c(2.0, 2.2, 2.4, 2.6, 2.8), c(2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 2.9), "fcr", 0.4)
  expect_equal(m$bias, 0.06)
  expect_equal(m$top_agree, 1)               # the two lowest FCR stay the lowest
  expect_equal(m$slope, 1, tolerance = 0.1)
  expect_equal(truncation_measures(1:2, c(NA, 1), "adg", 0.2)$n_lost, 1L)
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  expect_error(validate_truncation(v, settings = list(qc_config())), "named list")
  expect_error(validate_truncation(v, scenarios = "late"), "scenario")
  expect_error(validate_truncation(v, share = 0.8), "share")
  expect_error(validate_truncation(list()), "data.frame")
})
```
